detail.abstract: Environmental claims are easy to make and hard to verify. The FTC's 2012 Green Guides revision tightened the substantiation required for such claims, raising the value of claims firms can defend and the expected cost of claims they cannot. We measure green commercialization by applying large language models to the mandatory business description of 10-K filings, and compare consumer-facing industries, bound most strictly by the Guides, with other industries. The average effect is indistinguishable from zero, but the null masks opposite responses that hinge on ex ante credibility: previously unrated firms surface latent green activity, while firms with observably weak environmental ratings temper their claims. The same weak-rated firms compete on substance instead: green product patenting rises, and markup and gross profitability improve. Claims, once credible, are quickly imitated; verifiable products are not. A standard that makes green claims credible does not uniformly expand green commercialization; it reallocates green-market returns toward firms that respond on the investment margin.

title: Can Small-Scale Fisheries Improve Food Security under Climate Shocks? Evidence from Côte d’Ivoire
affiliations: Université Félix Houphouët-Boigny and Université Félix Houphouët-Boigny

detail.title: Can Small-Scale Fisheries Improve Food Security under Climate Shocks? Evidence from Côte d’Ivoire
detail.abstract: Small-scale fisheries are increasingly promoted as a policy instrument for improving food security and strengthening climate resilience across Sub-Saharan Africa. Yet whether participation in fishing itself improves household food security remains an open empirical question. Using nationally representative data from the 2021 Harmonized Household Living Conditions Survey (EHCVM) in Côte d’Ivoire, this study examines the relationships among fishing participation, fishing income, climate shocks, and household food insecurity, measured by the Food Insecurity Experience Scale (FIES). To address the non-random selection of households into fishing activities, we estimate treatment effects using an Inverse Probability Weighted Regression Adjustment (IPWRA) estimator, complemented by survey-weighted generalized linear models and robustness analyses. The results show that participation in small-scale fisheries does not significantly reduce household food insecurity after controlling for observable household characteristics. By contrast, higher fishing income is consistently associated with lower food insecurity, whereas climate shocks remain a strong and robust predictor of food insecurity across all model specifications. These findings indicate that the contribution of fisheries to food security depends less on participation itself than on the economic returns generated under climate-vulnerable conditions. The study contributes to the food policy literature by distinguishing livelihood participation from livelihood performance and by providing nationally representative evidence that fisheries improve food security only when they generate sustainable incomes. The findings suggest that fisheries policies should prioritize productivity, profitability, market integration, and climate resilience rather than simply expanding participation in fishing activities.

title: Apparentment as a Matching Market: The Division of the Surplus Seat
affiliations: London School of Economics & Political Science (LSE) - Department of Government

detail.title: Apparentment as a Matching Market: The Division of the Surplus Seat

declarations.declarationOfInterest: na

detail.abstract: Under a divisor method of apportionment, two lists may sign an apparentment: they pool into one list for the allocation, and a seat the pool wins is split between them by the same method. In several systems, notably the Knesset, each list may sign with at most one partner. We study the resulting cooperative problem, whose coalitional worths are fixed by the apportionment law and so are computable, not assumed. Existing treatments regard an alliance as a single actor and leave open two questions a list faces: the division of the seat and the matching of who pairs with whom. The seat goes to the more under-represented partner, so ex ante it is split by recipiency probabilities. The single-partner rule makes formation a matching market. Our main result is a separation theorem: when a bloc is fully cohesive, both lists value a joint seat equally, so partner choice turns only on the pool's win probability, independent of the division, and a stable matching exists; as cohesion falls, the division enters partner choice and stability can fail. The agreements forgone, with the computable win and recipiency probabilities, place the cohesion weights in an identified set. We calibrate on five Knesset elections: the apportionment is reproduced exactly, the division rule holds in every capture, and in half the seat goes to the fewer-voted partner, which a proportional split cannot produce.

title: Chronic Hazards to Human Capability: A Gap Analysis of AI Risk Instruments and the Criteria for an Alternative

detail.title: Chronic Hazards to Human Capability: A Gap Analysis of AI Risk Instruments and the Criteria for an Alternative

detail.abstract: Evidence is accumulating that routine use of artificial intelligence can degrade the human cognitive capability it was designed to assist. Documented effects include skill decay amongst experienced clinicians, degraded judgement under incorrect machine advice, reduced critical thinking and discernment and weaker cognitive engagement during AI-assisted work. AI-assisted performance can enable a person to meet or exceed their normal baseline ability as the underlying skill erodes, so self-assessment may register enhancement while unaided capability declines. This paper asks whether the main AI risk taxonomies, incident systems, governance frameworks, regulatory instruments and evaluation tools can identify, record and manage this class of harm. Nine coverage criteria were derived from the five properties of the harm class and the harm pathways identified in the evidence review, four of them stated as pairings of source condition and consequence. They were mapped against the MIT AI Risk Repository, the OECD incident framework and a wider corpus including the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, the EU AI Act, the UK framework, the United Nations advisory report, ISO/IEC 23894, ISO/IEC 42001, corporate-policy syntheses, safety benchmarks and major incident databases. The analysis finds that existing instruments recognise several adjacent consequences, but do not yet provide a dedicated longitudinal mechanism linking the source condition, cumulative exposure and unaided human-capability outcome. The paper therefore specifies the elements such a capability preservation layer would require: a condition-based hazard, a combination model, exposure and latency measures, capability and formation as harm categories and periodic measurement of unaided human performance.

title: Closing the GAAP: Copyright, Fair Use, and Public Access to FASB’s Accounting Standards Codification
affiliations: 273 Ventures

detail.title: Closing the GAAP: Copyright, Fair Use, and Public Access to FASB’s Accounting Standards Codification

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

keywords: and Public Access to FASB's Accounting Standards Codification accounting standards

detail.abstract: Should a teacher need permission to put an accounting rule on a lecture slide? Should an attorney be barred from linking to the text that supports their advice? The Financial Accounting Foundation's (FAF) access terms impose just such restrictions on generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP), which U.S. law requires public companies and many private businesses to follow. The Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) sets out those standards in its Accounting Standards Codification (ASC), and federal law references GAAP, FASB, or the ASC in over 800 sections across 39 titles of the CFR and 16 titles of the U.S. Code. That reach makes access to the ASC a question of public law across the economy. The text is needed before an organization even knows which rules govern it: current scope rules, exceptions, and effective dates tell it whether a Topic applies at all. Yet FAF's free viewer is licensed only for personal, non-commercial use. Controllers, auditors, advisers, and even educators cannot rely on that grant as permission for their professional use. Limits on preserving, linking to, and sharing the text make this first determination costlier, especially for smaller organizations that need outside advice. These access costs compound the compulsory issuer assessments that already fund standard setting, imposing an economic burden that spreads through prices, wages, and investment returns. This Article argues that the public must have access to the complete standards required both to determine its obligations and to comply with them. Both fair use and the courts' decisions on standards adopted into law support sharing that text in full. The public that must follow and finance these rules must also be free to preserve, share, study, and explain them.

title: Geometry from Histories: Categorical Reconstruction of Learned State Spaces
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Geometry from Histories: Categorical Reconstruction of Learned State Spaces

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: A state space reconstructed from histories must preserve the operations that give those histories their consequences. We formulate this requirement through a category of exact realizations of response laws and supported continuation. The complete response profile is terminal, and reduced exact realizations are therefore canonically isomorphic. A discounted operational metric gives a compact completion; finite-test approximation errors yield explicit Gromov-Hausdorff bounds with a separate term for unresolved continuation. Uniqueness also forces compatible local realizations to satisfy the cocycle condition. Temporal direction enters as an obstruction to representations that erase response-relevant order. Learned continuous-time signatures and attention provide a constructive realization whose compatibility can be examined under changes of recording and coordinates. ReLU components supply piecewise-affine local structure, with interface contributions retained by an exact distributional formula for finite contrasts. For systems with absorption, localization must intertwine killed continuation operators: this preserves termination laws, expected lifetime and transported responses, with quantitative bounds under approximate intertwining. Valuation and differential localization extend the construction when their additional operator hypotheses hold. The resulting framework reconstructs geometry through observable distinctions and specifies which dynamics and boundary effects must survive a change of representation.

title: Tackling the iceberg: addressing shared and private exposure in E-scooter safety analysis
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Ben-Gurion University of the Negev - Department of Industrial Engineering and Management and Israeli Traffic Police

detail.title: Tackling the iceberg: addressing shared and private exposure in E-scooter safety analysis
detail.abstract: The safety of e-scooters and appropriate policy tools for its containment attract ongoing debate and are challenged by a lack of exposure data. While operators of shared e-scooters provide highly granular telemetry, privately owned e-scooters exposure remains obscured. This study addresses this gap by developing a framework to estimate total vehicle-kilometers-travel exposure and analyzing localized crash risks. Utilizing a case study of Tel-Aviv, we combine empirical video traffic-counts with shared operations data to model total exposure across nine city quarters. An Empirical Bayes regression is then deployed to evaluate the combined effects of estimated VKT, bike-path-to-street-length ratios, and ownership mix, on localized accident rates. The results reveal distinct spatial dualities: shared e-scooters dominate the central business district, whereas the periphery is heavily dominated by privately-owned ones. The Empirical Bayes model demonstrates that the proposed exposure measure is appropriate. The cross-sectional model associates a 10% increase in bike-path density with localized accident reduction of 35%. These findings do not prove causality, but they do suggest that infrastructure improvements can be powerful interventions. In addition, high-traffic peripheral zones consistently exhibit elevated crash-to-exposure rates and positive Empirical Bayes residuals, possibly driven by unmonitored, faster privately-owned e-scooters use and lower infrastructure provisions. Furthermore, temporal anomalies indicate that exposure spikes - such as the openings of new mass transit stations - lead to accident surges if bike-path infrastructure is slow to respond. The study demonstrates that evaluating micromobility and specifically e-scooter safety as a homogenous system obscures spatial and ownership disparities. The findings provide planners with a predictive, exposure-weighted risk framework to optimize capital allocation, transitioning from reactive to proactive infrastructure expansion.

title: Here Comes the Signal: Mobile Internet and Deforestation in Brazil
affiliations: , University of Tübingen and Universitat de València

detail.title: Here Comes the Signal: Mobile Internet and Deforestation in Brazil

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced this study.
declarations.funderStatement: David Zuchowski acknowledges financial support from the Generalitat Valenciana through the BEST-2026 programme.

detail.abstract: Does high-speed mobile internet increase or reduce deforestation? We study this question in the Brazilian Amazon. To identify the effect, we exploit the staggered rollout of access to 3G and 4G across municipalities in the Amazon biome in a difference-indifferences design. We find that the arrival of high-speed mobile internet reduces forest clearing. Evidence on mechanisms suggests that this effect operates through a structural transformation of the local economy, rather than through changes in environmental enforcement or public attention. Greater connectivity reallocates land, labor, and credit away from agriculture and toward off-farm activities. Digital infrastructure can thus foster structural transformation while easing pressure on land, with lower deforestation emerging as an unintended by-product of local economic development.

title: FinRL-DeepSeek Revisited: A Reproduction and Multi-Seed Robustness Analysis of LLM-Infused Risk-Sensitive Trading Agents

detail.title: FinRL-DeepSeek Revisited: A Reproduction and Multi-Seed Robustness Analysis of LLM-Infused Risk-Sensitive Trading Agents

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was conducted as an academic project within an MSc program.

detail.abstract: We reproduce and extend FinRL-DeepSeek [Benhenda, 2025], a trading framework combining Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) [Schulman et al., 2017], Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) constraints [Rockafellar and Uryasev, 2000], and large language model (LLM) signals extracted from financial news. Using the Nasdaq-100 universe (2013-2023) and the agent-ready datasets released by the original authors, we implement four agents from scratch in PyTorch - PPO, CPPO, PPO-DeepSeek, and CPPO-DeepSeek - and backtest them on the 2019-2023 period against an equal-weight buy-and-hold baseline. On a single seed, our results replicate the qualitative pattern reported by Benhenda (2025): LLM infusion improves both return and Sharpe ratio for both the unconstrained and CVaR-constrained agents. However, extending the evaluation to two independent seeds - a small but motivating step in light of well-documented seed sensitivity in deep RL [Henderson et al., 2018] - suggests that this single-seed pattern may not be stable, particularly for PPO-DeepSeek, whose Sharpe ratio ranking relative to plain PPO reverses between the two seeds we test. In contrast, CPPO-DeepSeek shows the smallest spread in total return across our two seeds of any agent. We present these observations as preliminary evidence, not a settled finding, and argue that they motivate wider-scale multi-seed evaluation in financial reinforcement learning research, an area where single-seed backtests remain the norm. We release our full codebase, including the trading environment, PPO/CPPO implementations, and evaluation pipeline, to support reproducibility.

title: A Proxy for Risk-Adjusted Performance of Everyday Gambles
affiliations: Georgetown University - McDonough School of Business and Risktyle

detail.title: A Proxy for Risk-Adjusted Performance of Everyday Gambles

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicts

detail.abstract: The current literature on risk-adjusted performance is largely focused on calculating ratios like the Sharpe Ratio or performance measures like the Modigliani-Modigliani M-square on financial data. This involves converting a price series into a return series and then normalizing a numerator of expected or ex-post returns by some measure of risk-either volatility or drawdown. This calculation is done to help investors gauge the absolute or relative attractiveness of an investment opportunity either in isolation or relative to a benchmark. However, in other aspects of life, individuals are often faced with risky choices-whether it is a pure gamble (as in say a poker gamble or a bet on a sports team), or even on decisions as to whether to buy insurance for a car or a house. In this paper, we use the gambles proposed in Kahneman-Tversky's seminal 1979 paper to articulate a way in which a risk-adjusted measure can be created to evaluate the relative riskiness of a decision, based on a probability of an event, relative to the expected value of the gamble. We then test it on 14 original gambles proposed in the Kahneman-Tversky paper but also show how those same purely numerical gambles in the original paper might be represented in real life situations. Since the gambles are relatively simple with a probability and a payoff, the technique proposed here is a bit more complex and constrained relative to the relatively obvious measures in the financial performance industry.

detail.abstract: This paper is devoted to the execution of crude oil arbitrage and momentum strategies with volatility targeting by using Large Language Models (LLM), comparing efficiency and profitability of LLaMA2 and GPT3.5. The objective of this study is to estimate the impacts of oil price volatility on oil companies' strategic investments from a regional level. Therefore, oil price volatility should be an independent variable in the model equation. This method is consistent with earlier studies that investigate the relationship between uncertainty and investment in Tobin's q theory. Oil price uncertainty can arise from a number of different sources including global oil demand and supply conditions, the actions of institutional actors (OPEC), geopolitical issues (approximately 50 per cent of world proven oil reserves are located in just four countries in the Middle East), and speculation in oil future markets. The complicated elements contribute the oil price uncertainty to be high and hard to predict. Therefore, although high oil prices normally imply high profits for oil exploration and production companies, the uncertainty of price could still significantly impact their strategic investment decisions. Previous studies diversify their results in the shape of the relationship between oil price uncertainty and investment. For instance, studies such as Mohn & Misund (2009) and Elder & Serietis (2010) find a linear relationship between oil price uncertainty and investment; while Henriques & Sadorsky (2011) found a Ucurve relationship. Therefore, in this study, the variable of oil price volatility square will be introduced as an optional variable. If the specification of model with the variable shows a better result than the one without it, then the shape of the relationship would be a curve line. Volatility targeting is a portfolio management tool aimed at managing portfolio risk by targeting a particular volatility level and adjusting the positioning of the portfolio in an attempt to stay close to the volatility target. Although it is possible to implement volatility targeting with any asset, portfolios of derivatives provide a cost-effective implementation as trading is often done on a daily basis. Following the research of Moreira and Muir (2017) the idea is very straightforward; one needs to simply scale asset weights in the portfolio by the ratio of the target volatility and the expectation of future volatility given the current asset mix. Obviously, the value of the targeting is greatly impacted by the quality of the volatility expectation model, but since these estimates are over short horizons, the fact that volatility tends to cluster makes this an "easier" effort. In equation form, the return of the volatility managed portfolio, is the volatility scaled return of the unmanaged portfolio which is simply the sum product of the asset weights and their returns. Crude oil is a pivotal global commodity whose price fluctuations permeate the broader economy through channels such as transportation costs, energy-weighted inflation indices, and corporate procurement and inventory strategies. Accurate forecasting of oil prices, even for single-step daily predictions, holds significant practical value. Marginal but consistent accuracy gains around price turning points can substantially mitigate risks associated with supply disruptions and excessive hedging costs. However, the inherent characteristics of oil markets-such as fat-tailed residuals, volatility clustering, asymmetric responses to supply and demand shocks, and frequent structural breaks-pose considerable challenges to traditional linear models. While classical time series approaches like ARIMA and exponential smoothing capture low-frequency trends, they often fall short in modeling the complex, nonlinear interactions among inventory levels, convenience yields, market expectations, and geopolitical risks. Although regime-switching models introduce nonlinearity, their reliance on strong assumptions regarding the number of states and transition mechanisms limits their applicability during unconventional events. detail.abstract: This paper studies whether arbitrage frictions transmit across otherwise distinct trades. I exploit the settlement mismatch created by the 2024 US transition to T+1, while many foreign securities held by US-listed cross-border ETFs continued to settle on T+2. Relative to non-US ETFs tracking the same indices, primary-market arbitrage, measured by flow-mispricing responsiveness, declines among directly exposed cross-border ETFs. The decline appears primarily in creations and generally grows with portfolio exposure to T+2-settled securities. Exposed ETFs also tilt toward T+1-settled securities, experience higher tracking error, and become less liquid. Domestic ETFs face no direct settlement mismatch, yet their flow-mispricing responsiveness declines more when their predetermined reliance on authorized participants (APs) active in cross-border ETFs is greater. The decline associated with this indirect exposure is smaller when AP balance-sheet capacity is greater and larger when poor netting coincides with high global exposure. These findings suggest that market segmentation need not contain a local arbitrage friction when distinct trades draw on shared intermediary capacity.

detail.abstract: Political polarization is widely documented, yet we know less about how elite polarization accumulates inside representative institutions over time, and whether long-run increases reflect replacement (the entry of more extreme legislators) or adaptation (within-legislator positional change). Using roll-call votes from the Chilean Chamber of Deputies across six legislative periods (2002-2026) and dynamically anchored ideal-point estimates on a common scale, this article traces secular changes in revealed ideology and decomposes rising extremity into compositional turnover versus within-legislator movement. Polarization, measured as average absolute distance from a fixed reference point, increased by approximately 76% between legislative periods 2002-06 and 2022-26, with no evidence of sharp discontinuities around relevant political events. New entrants are, on average, more extreme than incumbents, while the within-legislator specification shows no systematic increase in extremity after entry. A replacement-only counterfactual that holds legislators fixed at their entry extremity reproduces essentially the entire observed increase, indicating that long-run polarization is descriptively accounted for by cumulative compositional replacement rather than systematic within-legislator adaptation.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether international reserves nonlinearly condition the relationship between global financial risk and the share of foreign portfolio equity investment in total foreign equity investment (FPIS). Using an annual panel of 110 countries over 2001-2020, the baseline results show that higher international reserves relative to total financial liabilities to nonresidents (RES) are associated with a larger FPIS, particularly among emerging market and developing economies (EMDEs), while higher global financial risk, proxied by the VIX index, is associated with a lower FPIS. Beyond these baseline results, panel threshold regressions locate the relevant RES threshold for EMDEs at approximately 9.5%, above which the adverse VIX-FPIS association is about 68% smaller. State-dependent local projections provide complementary evidence of smaller and less persistent adverse FPIS responses to increases in the VIX in the high-RES regime.

detail.abstract: AbstractWe study how a negative shock to future profitability in the fossil energy supply chain affects firms’ direction of innovation. We propose a novel approach to measure firms’ exposure to the 2014 oil price collapse, and find that more exposed firms significantly increased clean R&D relative to less exposed peers. The results suggest that firms in the fossil energy supply chain possess transferable capabilities for clean innovation, and that declining fossil profitability can accelerate the clean transition not only by shifting resources away from fossil activities, but also by redirecting innovation within exposed firms towards clean technologies.

detail.abstract: This short announcement introduces two new open-source software packages, hitsr for R and hitspy for Python, implementing the HITS algorithm for fast and deterministic Maximum Score Estimation (MSE) in binary choice models. The packages provide a practical, scalable, and reproducible alternative to traditional parametric estimators such as logit and probit. Their design is based on the algorithmic framework presented in Florios, Louka & Bilias (2025, SoftwareX), which demonstrated that tabu-based global optimization can solve the MSE problem efficiently even for large sample size n and number of parameters p. The purpose of this note is to make the econometrics and machine learning communities aware of these tools and to facilitate adoption of MSE in empirical research.

detail.abstract: The institution that adopts a rule, the institution that applies it, and the institution empowered to change its legal basis need not coincide. This Essay argues that municipal legal review remains incomplete until it connects an identified external dependency to a response within the relevant institution's authority. It develops that argument through a comparative doctrinal analysis of eight federal appellate decisions issued between July and September 2026, concentrated in environmental and energy regulation. The analysis distinguishes interpretive, enforcement, forum, and temporal dependency, treating temporal dependency as a dimension that crosses the others. Across these settings, identifying a legal problem does not establish that the municipality can correct it through drafting or a change in enforcement. Conversely, a judgment sustaining an external rule can leave significant local questions unresolved. The contribution is an account of how the allocation of authority limits the available response, connecting a dependency's legal source to the actor able to address it. This extends the application and reassessment process within Judicial Impact Assessment (JIA).

title: The Primacy of the Replication Portfolio Rate in Modern Option Pricing Theory
affiliations: University of Toledo

detail.title: The Primacy of the Replication Portfolio Rate in Modern Option Pricing Theory

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none
declarations.funderStatement: none

detail.abstract: Traditional derivatives theory relies on an artificial "implied volatility smile" to reconcile the systemic mis-pricing of out-of-the-money (OTM) options. This paper presents a streamlined, scale-invariant alternative that shifts the analytical focus back to the foundational mechanic of derivatives theory: the internal funding rate of the replication portfolio. Both the Black-Scholes (1973) model and the Moore model (2003) use the Fokker-Planck solution to model options. The drift rate is the rate derived from the portfolio of the replication portfolio. Under strict asset equivalence constraints, the artificial volatility smile vanishes into a flat single variance baseline. What emerges natively is Moore's R, the true replication vector demanded by the system's solution equation. Rather than a flat profile, Moore's R is close to the macroeconomic risk-free rate through in-the-money (ITM) options, but drops precipitously in an exponential pattern outof-the-money. The replication portfolio rate model contains the stock returns rate as a significant rate. Interestingly, the pattern can be found in the MacBeth and Merville (1979) paper easily if one looks. When solved, the stock return rate can be shown to converge to a single rate across all options in the chain. The approach is completely validated with great precision, and the reader will agree with the author that the Fokker-Planck Equation Solution using a rate equal to the rate earned on the replication portfolio is the correct use of the simple form of the Fokker-Planck envelope. It fits extremely well and is consistent with modern portfolio theory. Robustness validation across independent linear averages, scale-free ratios, and pre-log combined portfolios reveals that while raw empirical configurations carry authentic tracking noise, the underlying framework achieves exceptionally high aggregate convergence, confirming that the orthodox volatility smile is merely a symptom of an incorrect assumption. The drift rate is not the risk-free rate; rather, it is the rate derived from the portfolio of the replication portfolio. This orientation solves many of the enigmas in modern contingent claims research and is one of the most significant findings in the area.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the scope for diversification in U.S. imports of bulk antibiotic active pharmaceutical ingredients (API) by estimating source-specific sourcing relationships for China and the rest of the world (ROW). Using quarterly U.S. customs data from 2002Q1 to 2026Q2, the analysis estimates restricted rank-one vector error-correction models that treat prices, quantities, and import expenditure as jointly endogenous. The main result is a pronounced asymmetry in long-run cross-price responsiveness: a 1 percent increase in ROW unit values is associated with a 1.28 percent increase in Chinese import quantities, whereas a 1 percent increase in Chinese unit values is associated with only a 0.09 percent increase in ROW quantities. A conservative bootstrap comparison rejects equality of these coefficients at the nominal 5 percent level, and both sources exhibit negative own-price relationships. The results indicate uneven effective substitutability across sources, consistent with differences in procurement costs and other sourcing conditions. For governments and firms pursuing diversification, the findings underscore that geographic diversification and effective substitutability are distinct dimensions of supply security: alternative suppliers may exist without being equally able to accommodate changes in demand at competitive cost.

detail.abstract: This white paper introduces the Trauma-Informed Screening Protocol (TISP), the sixth framework developed under the Royalty Institute for Trauma-Informed Practice. TISP responds to a documented and sustained pattern in Ontario school boards in which Black students are suspended and expelled at rates far higher than their share of the student population, a pattern that has persisted through years of anti-racism training, public apologies, and data collection. TISP proposes a required trauma screening step, completed before any discretionary suspension or expulsion is finalized, so that a student's behavior is assessed for underlying trauma before a punitive consequence is applied. TISP is introduced publicly through the Pause and Ask campaign, developed by Royalty Helping Hands (RHH), a federally incorporated nonprofit based in Toronto with an existing contracted relationship with the Toronto District School Board and the Peel District School Board through the My Black Is Whole program. This paper sets out the data supporting the need for TISP, the structure of the protocol, its place among RHH's frameworks, and a proposed pilot pathway. TISP is filed under RHH's ORCID and Zenodo scholarly record and is prepared for submission to the Education Resources Information Center (ERIC) as an original, Canadian-developed contribution to trauma-informed school discipline practice.

title: Not Poor, Still Powerless: Ideology and the Psychology of Saving Inhibition
affiliations: University of Granada and University of Granada - Department of Economic Theory and History

detail.title: Not Poor, Still Powerless: Ideology and the Psychology of Saving Inhibition

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: Ana I. Moro-Egido acknowledges financial support from the Spanish Ministry of Science and Innovation (grant number PID2022-137819NB-I00) and the Regional Government of Andalusia and the FEDER (grant B-SEJ-10‐UGR20, DGP-PIDI-2024-00544). Francisco Rodriguez acknowledges financial support from FUNCAS

detail.abstract: Why do households fail to save even when they want to? This paper defines saving inhibition as the gap between desired and realized saving and studies its determinants using nationally representative survey data from Spain. We develop a unified intertemporal model that integrates liquidity constraints, present bias, self-control costs, and attention frictions with a novel belief-driven channel: politically-structured perceptions of public insurance that shift the effective cost of private saving. Three main findings emerge. First, economic constraints operate asymmetrically: liquidity constraints suppress realized saving, while income risk primarily increases saving inhibition, reflecting frustrated precautionary motives that cannot be acted upon. Second, self-control problems are the single largest predictor of the saving gap (marginal effect 0.306-0.318, robust to IV), yet leave realized saving unaffected-a clean separation between intentions and actions that standard models cannot capture. Third, politically structured beliefs about the role of the state shape saving behavior independently of income and controls: support for welfare and environmental spending reduces saving, while support for defense spending and negative state attribution substantially increase saving across all dimensions. Strikingly, left-right self-placement becomes insignificant once these beliefs are included, indicating that the ideological gradient operates through substantive beliefs rather than partisan identity. A two-stage IV strategy with Kleibergen-Paap F = 39.75 and a non-rejected Hansen J test (p = 0.223) supports the causal interpretation.

title: Decision-Disclosure Coupling in the Three-Prisoners Problem: A Reappraisal of the 1/2 Posterior

detail.title: Decision-Disclosure Coupling in the Three-Prisoners Problem: A Reappraisal of the 1/2 Posterior

detail.abstract: The three-prisoners problem is a classical example in which posterior inference depends on the protocol governing the warden's announcement. We study a structural extension in which the objective mechanism selecting the pardoned prisoner, d, is linked to the nontrivial disclosure probability by q = ψ(d). We distinguish this decision mechanism from prisoner A's subjective prior µ. For a reported posterior p = P d µ (S = A | M = b), with µ A , µ C > 0, the compatible decision mechanisms are exactly ψ-1 (︃ pµ C (1-p)µ A)︃. Thus, conditional on a known prior and coupling, structural identification is governed by the fibers of ψ. We then reappraise the author's 2014 model. Its posterior admits a unique prior-independent scalar factorization through ψ 14 (θ, ρ, τ) = θ + τ 1 + θ. Interior fibers of ψ 14 are line segments, while q = 0 and q = 1 have singleton fibers. With equal subjective prior weights on A and C, a posterior of 1/2 requires q = 1, which under ψ 14 identifies (θ, ρ, τ) = (0, 0, 1). Under prior calibration µ = d with θ, τ > 0, the same half posterior is instead characterized by τ = θ 2. The analysis clarifies how the same numerical posterior can encode different underlying decision-disclosure structures.

title: Poverty Luxury: Law, Marketing, and Advertising in the Commodification of Scarcity and the Social Production of Consumer Desire

detail.title: Poverty Luxury: Law, Marketing, and Advertising in the Commodification of Scarcity and the Social Production of Consumer Desire

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author(s) declare(s) that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract: Consumer-protection law regulates "vulnerability" through enumerated categorical traits-age, infirmity, credulity, disability-that a trader could reasonably foresee. This article argues that this categorical architecture systematically fails to reach a distinct and empirically documented harm: the commercial exploitation of economic scarcity itself as a psychological lever to intensify consumer desire, particularly through marketing techniques that graft luxury and status signaling onto credit products, discount framing, and manufactured urgency cues aimed at low-income consumers. Drawing on comparative analysis of the European Union's Unfair Commercial Practices Directive, United States Federal Trade Commission unfairness doctrine, United Kingdom financial-conduct regulation of the "poverty premium," Brazilian consumer-protection law, South Africa's National Credit Act, and Australian Consumer Law enforcement against manufactured scarcity cues, the article identifies what it terms a "vulnerability-vector mismatch": doctrinal triggers for heightened scrutiny track demographic and cognitive status rather than the structural condition of economic precarity that scarcity-based marketing is functionally designed to exploit. Brazil's Consumer Defense Code, which recognizes "condição social" as an independent ground of abusive practice, is examined as a comparative outlier demonstrating that the mismatch is not conceptually inevitable. The article situates this doctrinal gap against the sociological and behavioral literature on poverty premiums, conspicuous consumption, and manufactured scarcity, and proposes an Economic Vulnerability and Scarcity Authenticity Standard that would extend heightened scrutiny to demonstrably targeted scarcity marketing while preserving the doctrinal distinction between authentic and manufactured urgency. The article confronts institutional-capacity and administrability objections to this proposal directly and identifies the conditions under which the thesis would be falsified. AI Disclosure Statement: During the preparation of this manuscript, the author used AI-based language and research-assistance tools for drafting support, research organization, literature discovery, analytical structuring, and language refinement. The author critically reviewed, edited, verified, and assumed responsibility for all legal analysis, argumentation, sources, interpretations, data, and conclusions contained in the final manuscript.

title: Beyond Station Rankings: Comparing Metrorail Access and Transit Depth Across the Washington, DC Region

detail.title: Beyond Station Rankings: Comparing Metrorail Access and Transit Depth Across the Washington, DC Region

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have influenced the work reported in this publication.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract:
Conventional Metrorail rankings compare individual stations. They measure recorded station use but do not capture the transit depth of an urban district whose entries are distributed among closely spaced stations and whose overlapping pedsheds create urban-district-scale access. Although regional agencies recognize that stations differ, the frameworks reviewed from the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority (WMATA), DC Office of Planning (DCOP), and Metropolitan Washington Council of Governments (MWCOG), including the National Capital Region Transportation Planning Board (TPB), do not provide a standard, reproducible measure that combines multiple stations, public entrances, overlapping pedsheds, scheduled route access, aggregate matched-period station entries, and surrounding structural concentration at the urban-district scale.

This publication makes the urban district the unit of analysis. It measures transit depth through station and entrance density, overlap among official WMATA Metrorail station pedsheds, scheduled line-label access, route choice, and aggregate station entries. It then relates those independently measured transit conditions to Structural Intensity, the publication's measure of built-form concentration. The fixed analysis compares urban districts in Washington, DC, Northern Virginia, and Maryland; the Foggy Bottom–West End western-extension sensitivity, Greater Central DC, and the Rosslyn–Ballston Corridor are reported separately as sensitivity geographies.

Traditional Downtown DC occupies the highest measured tier. It contains 10 interior stations, 23 public entrance facilities, all six scheduled Metrorail line labels, and 92.3 percent of its land within at least two official station pedsheds. Extended Functional Downtown DC retains majority multi-station coverage at 70.9 percent. Clarendon is an independent majority-overlap exception at 50.3 percent, but it remains a one-station urban district with one public entrance facility served by two scheduled line labels. Traditional Downtown DC recorded 105,387 average weekday station entries during the matched January 2-May 8, 2026 period; Southwest BID recorded the highest fixed independent total at 29,049.

The Foggy Bottom–West End western-extension sensitivity confirms that majority overlapping access remains when the fixed downtown boundary is expanded. Greater Central DC retains majority land overlap at 58.2 percent, and 61.6 percent of its qualifying Structural Intensity cells lie within at least two station pedsheds. No independent comparison urban district reproduces the downtown systems' combined scale of stations, entrances, scheduled route access, matched-period entries, structural concentration, and pervasive overlap. These results measure observed station use and spatial access, not passenger loads, platform throughput, service headroom, or operating reserve.

title: The University after AI

detail.title: The University after AI

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none
declarations.funderStatement: none

detail.abstract: This paper develops an analytic framework to offer strategic guidance to rebuild or reform universities through the AI era. We review the history of universities, the history of technology in universities, the economics of AI, and the economics of the university in order to combine these analytic perspectives into a framework to identify the main impact pathways of disruption of the university after AI. Universities have been impacted by technology before, with little effect. This time is different. Earlier waves lowered the cost of content, but content is not and has never been the core business of the university, which is matching and verification. Universities are multi-sided markets whose strategic asset is a credible warrant of quality over a credence good and AI is the first technology to disrupt this core function. We propose a range of strategic implications, both defensive and offensive, to deal with this disruption.

title: Unintended Consequence Of Waste Import Ban: A Story Of Export Quality Upgrading In Downstream Industries
affiliations: Guangzhou University

detail.title: Unintended Consequence Of Waste Import Ban: A Story Of Export Quality Upgrading In Downstream Industries
detail.abstract: Global waste trade is a concern in the world. As the largest developing country, China used to be the largest importer of wastes, which caused serious environmental damages. Waste import ban is an effective way to improve domestic environment quality. However, as typical wastes, importing waste plastics are important source of intermediate inputs for downstream industries. Given that the import shock of intermediate inputs significantly affects export quality, does waste import ban have unintended effects on export quality in downstream industries? In this study, I construct a theoretical model, and distinguish between high-income and low-income export destinations to analyze the differentiated effects of waste import ban. Then, I regard the import ban of waste plastics of China as a quasi-natural experiment. I design a difference-in-difference-in-difference (DDD) model, and employ product-industry-province-destination-year-level data for empirical analyses. I find that waste import ban leads to product quality upgrading in downstream industries of exporting to high-income countries, while it cannot significantly improve product quality of exporting to low-income countries. For high-income export destinations, this ban drives export quality upgrading by the mechanism of increasing R&D investment. The mechanism of changing quality of intermediate inputs does not play a role. Expanded analyses show that for segmented high-income countries, the impacts of this ban are differentiated. Except for downstream industries, this ban improves export quality of plastic industry. In addition, this ban reduces frontier distance of export quality (especially for high-income export destinations). In general, this study is the first to provide theory and evidence for the relationship between waste import ban and export quality, and also provide important implications for developing countries.

title: Geopolitical Supply-Chain Vulnerability and Relative Sectoral Equity Returns: Evidence from U.S. Strategic Dependence on China ⋆

detail.abstract: Against the background of rising geopolitical fragmentation, this paper examines whether financial markets price changes in U.S. strategic import vulnerability to China across upstream and downstream industries in the United States and China. We combine monthly Structural Strategic Import Risk Index (SSIRI) measures for 2004-2025 with publicly available U.S. and Chinese sectoral equity data. The analysis uses standardized monthly changes, Newey-West inference, extensive financial and global-risk controls, and false-discovery-rate corrections. A one-standard-deviation increase in exposure-weighted critical-minerals and advancedmaterials SSIRI is associated with a 1.10 percentage-point increase in the one-month U.S. upstream-minus-downstream return spread observed two months after the signal. A related 1.07 percentage-point three-month response appears in China. Decomposition results indicate an upstream-led U.S. response and a combination of stronger upstream and weaker downstream performance in China. Exposure-weighted SSIRI is more precisely related to equity returns than the equal-family structural measure. U.S. battery-sector results are generally null, while Chinese battery results are sensitive to portfolio construction. The findings reveal a sectorspecific association between strategic import vulnerability and relative equity returns.

title: The Joint Test the DC Height Study Did Not Complete: Institutional Divergence, Viewshed Sequencing, and the 2012–2013 Washington, DC Height Master Plan Review

detail.title: The Joint Test the DC Height Study Did Not Complete: Institutional Divergence, Viewshed Sequencing, and the 2012–2013 Washington, DC Height Master Plan Review

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have influenced the work reported in this publication.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract:
This standalone retrospective research brief examines the institutional structure, analytical sequencing, and scenario construction of the 2012–2013 National Capital Planning Commission–District of Columbia Height Master Plan review.

The congressional request initiated a jointly conducted review, and the agencies subsequently defined federal–local consensus and a jointly prepared master plan identifying where additional building height might be appropriate as the expected outcome. NCPC and the District completed substantial collaborative technical work, public engagement, economic analysis, and visual modeling. The process nevertheless culminated in separate federal and District reports containing materially different recommendations.

The brief evaluates whether the review completed a jointly approved, spatially explicit test of its strongest potential middle alternative: define and map agreed primary viewsheds and other protected geography first, identify the legally and physically plausible geography remaining after those exclusions, and evaluate selective additional height only within that residual area.

The documentary and spatial audit finds that NCPC performed a partial federal-side screen that removed certain viewshed streets, Pennsylvania Avenue, and streets in historic districts from its ratio analysis. The reviewed public record, however, does not demonstrate that NCPC and the District jointly approved that exclusion geography or integrated it with the study’s selective-height modeling, economic analysis, capacity measures, and final institutional findings.

The conclusion is methodological rather than pro- or anti-height. The brief does not allege bad faith, deny that interagency collaboration occurred, claim that Congress legislatively required a joint final report, or establish that a selective-height policy would necessarily produce meaningful development or public benefits. It identifies what the published review completed, what remained institutionally unreconciled, and how an exclusion-first test could structure any renewed Height Act analysis.

title: THE ONTOLOGY OF MONEY  - Trust, Monetary Illusion, and the Hidden Transfer of Purchasing Power

detail.title: THE ONTOLOGY OF MONEY  - Trust, Monetary Illusion, and the Hidden Transfer of Purchasing Power

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or non-financial interests that could have influenced the research, analysis, or conclusions presented in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: The abandonment of the gold standard in 1971 marked not merely a policy shift but a fundamental transformation in the ontology of money. Money transitioned from a representation of a scarce commodity to a trust-based nominal claim. This paper argues that this transition introduced two structural vulnerabilities: the risk of a collapse of trust and the risk of the abuse of trust. While the former manifests as visible monetary crises, the latter manifests as a subtle "monetary illusion" wherein nominal indicators improve while real purchasing power deteriorates. By examining the epistemological limitations of using a changing monetary unit to measure economic performance, this paper introduces the concept of the "Monetary Measurement Paradox" and the "Silent Monetary Tax." It concludes that the sustainability of fiat money depends not only on institutional credibility but also on the ethical management of the trust constraint. This paper is a conceptual analysis and does not employ empirical data, relying instead on deductive reasoning and ontological inquiry into monetary economics.

title: Lighter Capital, Heavier Household Finance

detail.title: Lighter Capital, Heavier Household Finance

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study uses aggregate and publicly available secondary data and does not involve human-subject intervention.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Information technologies can expand productive capacity without easing household financial or fiscal pressures. This paper compares household financial assets and business nonfinancial assets relative to consumption in the United States, China, Japan, and Germany. Financial assets rise relative to consumption in all four samples, while business assets decline relative to household finance; the United States also shows a long-run decline in capital relative to consumption. Issuer-side accounts connect these movements to business valuation, household credit, net foreign assets, and net government liabilities. U.S. and Japanese evidence shows declining broad-household financial shares, while U.S. resource balances and financial-gain diagnostics favor the top. These patterns motivate a conditional adjustment logic: government balance sheets can bridge adjustment when private and external channels are constrained, while stronger earnings, insurance, and asset participation can reduce repeated financing pressures. This framework offers a common direction for the United States and China without requiring convergence of ownership systems.

title: Has climate change optimism improved or declined over time? The role of board independence
affiliations: Sasin GIBA, Mahidol University International College (MUIC) and Pennsylvania State University - School of Graduate Professional Studies (SGPS)

detail.title: Has climate change optimism improved or declined over time? The role of board independence

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: We analyze the evolution of climate change sentiment in firms over time and the role of independent directors using sentiment metrics developed by Sautner et al. (2023). These metrics, derived from advanced textual analysis of earnings calls, capture overall sentiment, positive sentiment, negative sentiment, and specific metrics for physical risk, regulatory risk, and new business opportunities. Our findings reveal a positive trend in sentiment, driven by increased optimism and reduced negativity. Regulatory risk sentiment shows rising optimism, while physical risk sentiment remains stable. Independent directors initially dampen optimism, but this diminishes over time, highlighting sustainability's strategic value. These findings suggest that climate-related corporate communication is increasingly driven by long-term strategic and economic considerations rather than symbolic statements. The results demonstrate the role of governance in shaping how firms respond to sustainability challenges, with implications for corporate strategy, investor assessment of climate disclosures, and regulatory policy design.

title: Evaluating National R&D Intensity: Trade Openness, Absorptive Capacity, Curvature Reversal, and Long-Run Economic Performance across 72 Countries
affiliations: KISTEP Korea Institute of S&T Evalution and Planning and Georgia Institute of Technology

detail.title: Evaluating National R&D Intensity: Trade Openness, Absorptive Capacity, Curvature Reversal, and Long-Run Economic Performance across 72 Countries

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Authors declare no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: Korea Institute of Science and Technology Evaluation and Planning (KISTEP) funded this research.

detail.abstract: National R&D intensity targets are widely used to guide investment in technological capability, yet they often presume that additional R&D has a similar economic relationship across countries. We develop a regime-based framework for evaluating how trade openness changes the slope and curvature of the association between national R&D intensity and long-run economic performance, and how human capital-based absorptive capacity conditions that reconfiguration. Using a 31-year panel (1987-2017) of 72 developed and developing countries, we estimate heterogeneous longrun relationships while accounting for common global shocks. The unconditional estimates do not provide precise evidence of an inverted-U relationship. Once trade openness is considered, a systematic conditional pattern emerges. At lower and moderate openness, the relationship is concave: greater openness weakens the association at very low R&D intensity but attenuates diminishing returns at higher intensity, shifting the estimated maximum to the right. At sufficiently high openness, conditional curvature becomes positive, eliminating the interior maximum; a Ushaped relationship with an interior minimum appears only when the low-R&D slope is negative and the minimum lies within the observed range. Cross-group comparisons indicate a larger curvature shift in lower human capital economies, although the statistical evidence is less robust and sensitive to the inclusion of country-specific trends. The study contributes to technology impact evaluation by showing that national R&D intensity is not an independently interpretable input indicator: its long-run association with economic performance depends on global integration and domestic absorptive or learning capacity. R&D targets should be used as conditional planning diagnostics rather than universal prescriptions.

title: Gate Design and Stage-Dependent Incentives in Retail Proprietary-Trading Evaluations: Why Passing Is Not Standalone Evidence of Skill, and Why the Product Fails to Pay Under Measured Trading Constraints
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Gate Design and Stage-Dependent Incentives in Retail Proprietary-Trading Evaluations: Why Passing Is Not Standalone Evidence of Skill, and Why the Product Fails to Pay Under Measured Trading Constraints

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no financial or personal relationship with any of the firms named in this paper, and has not received compensation from any party in connection with it. The author has purchased evaluation accounts from firms in this sector in the past as a participant; no such account was active during the research period, and no account-level data from those purchases is used here.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. Market data was purchased by the author; total data expenditure is reported in Section 2.

detail.abstract:
Retail proprietary-trading firms sell a two-stage product: a paid evaluation that must reach a profit target before breaching a trailing drawdown, followed by a funded account that must survive a minimum window and satisfy a consistency rule before a payout is released. We show that the geometry of this contract creates incentives that differ by stage and that make passing a poor standalone signal of skill. Under end-of-day trailing the evaluation rewards a fast, lumpy trade cadence while the funded account punishes it, by a factor of nine in the joint gate at identical strategy parameters. The evaluation is defeatable at zero skill: position sizing alone yields a pass probability near 0.40, against a measured cohort rate of 0.168. Pass probability does rise with skill, but at a fixed cadence a real edge and aggressive sizing move it by nearly the same amount, so a pass rate confounds the two and cannot by itself be read as evidence of skill. And under a simplified contract model the seller's contribution margin is bounded by the gap between perceived and actual gate probabilities — the probability analogue of shrouding a price component — under which a permeable, marketed evaluation and a hard, unpriceable payout gate are what a margin-maximising seller would choose. The observed design is consistent with that: across the sector, pass rates are published far more often than payout rates, and two families of firms with inverted rule architectures differ by a factor of 1.7 in pass rate within a single sample, an association consistent with substitution between gates rather than with skill filtering.

The same geometry produces negative expected value for the participant. Within the strategy universe we measured, and under the trade-level cost model the paper relies on, no measured strategy configuration at the drifts we observed clears break-even on any account structure we could source: a transaction-cost floor exceeded every gross per-trade edge surviving our pre-specified research protocol, and the joint pass-and-payout gate is compressed to at or below the line implied by the account price. Under the baseline simulation model, break-even lies between a 40.5% and 41.5% win rate at 1:1.5 net of costs across the three accounts studied in detail and the two implementations, against a driftless baseline of 40.0%. We also measure the delta-neutral construction these firms prohibit and find it approximately expected-value neutral under symmetric sizing at the observed payout ceiling, with the ceiling rather than the prohibition doing the work. Every account-level result is reported against a zero-edge control through the identical pipeline, without which pass and payout rates are uninterpretable.

title:
Machine Contact Layer 
Transport-Independent Contact and Continuity for Machine Communication

detail.title:
Machine Contact Layer 
Transport-Independent Contact and Continuity for Machine Communication

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author leads OJOBIT Applied R&D Lab, which developed the Machine Contact Layer. No other conflicts of interest are declared.
declarations.funderStatement: The research was self-funded by the author and OJOBIT Applied R&D Lab.

detail.abstract:
Machines increasingly communicate across heterogeneous networks, radios, vendors, operating systems, and trust domains, yet most communication stacks assume that a usable bearer or prior relationship already exists. This paper introduces the Machine Contact Layer (MCL), a transport-independent architecture for establishing, maintaining, validating, refusing, migrating, and handing off machine-to-machine communication contact without conflating contact with identity, authentication, authority, trust, or permission to act.

MCL separates semantic objects, canonical wire representation, contact and session state, transport bindings, and the machine-facing integration boundary. It supports both regular communication over an existing bearer and optional zero-prior contact in which machines establish minimal reachability and negotiate a continuation path. The reference implementation targets freestanding C99 with caller-owned memory and has been exercised across IP, Bluetooth Low Energy, acoustic bootstrap, Windows and Android hosts, and ESP32-S3-class embedded hardware.

Experimental evaluation preserved one logical contact through 104 physical-medium changes, including 100 alternating BLE/IP migrations, with 2,989 recorded checks and zero failures. Separate zero-prior hardware experiments completed acoustic rendezvous, candidate validation, local policy admission, and BLE migration in both derived BLE role orientations. A bounded three-machine shared-air experiment further showed that a competing proposal did not replace the selected transaction.

The contribution is not a new radio, discovery mechanism, or application protocol, but a compact interoperability boundary that preserves communication continuity across changing bearers while keeping security, policy, and application semantics explicitly separate. MCL is intended to provide a small, inspectable foundation for more predictable and interoperable communication among heterogeneous machines operating in increasingly machine-dense environments.

title: India's 10-Year Government Bond Market and Global Financial Linkages: A Comparative Study Amid the Russia-Ukraine War and Middle East Conflicts

detail.abstract: This study examines the relationship between the 10-year government bond market of India and selected 10-year government bond markets of the world during the period 2021-2025. The study covers India, the USA, the UK, Japan, Australia, Brazil and South Africa, which represent major developed and emerging economies from different regions of the world. To understand the behavior, co-movement and influence of international bond markets on India's 10-year government bond returns, the monthly bond returns are analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson's correlation coefficient analysis and Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression. The study period is important because it spans several major global economic and geopolitical events, such as the post-COVID recovery, the Russia-Ukraine war, the Israel-Gaza conflict, and wider tensions in the Middle East. Moreover, these developments brought about changes in global inflation, interest rates, energy prices, investor confidence and capital flows, and hence the period is an important one for studying international bond-market linkages.

detail.abstract: We provide an introduction to real-world asset (RWA) tokenization, and develop two economic models connecting this emerging market to classical financial theory. In search for a theory of RWA tokenization, we classify RWA tokenization according to the role of the underlying asset, distinguishing standard RWA tokenization, stablecoins, and Digital Asset Treasuries (DATs). Our first model connects tokenization with security design under asymmetric information. Continuous secondary-market trading generates information recovery, reducing adverse-selection costs over time and affecting both the issuance price and the optimal tokenization design. Our second model develops a dynamic corporate-finance framework for DATs, in which market valuation, capital-market financing, and crypto accumulation interact endogenously. We characterize the optimal issuance policy and illustrate the model using Strategy as a case study. A few directions for future research are discussed, providing a starting point for further theoretical and empirical study of RWA markets.

detail.abstract: Fraud of this kind needs staff. That obvious fact has attracted almost no research attention, largely because the people who do the work sit in a jurisdiction the victim-country literature cannot enter. This paper approaches transnational call-centre fraud as an employment problem before it is a criminological one. It draws on six enforcement operations mounted between August 2023 and August 2025 by the Gautam Buddh Nagar Police Commissionerate in India's National Capital Region, which dismantled call centres defrauding victims in the United States and the United Kingdom and produced 282 arrests. The author held supervisory charge of crime in that commissionerate for part of the period. The central finding concerns who was in the room. Arrest records across the corpus disclose two geographically distinct recruitment pools, an age distribution beginning at eighteen and clustering heavily in the early twenties, and residential concentration in a handful of Delhi localities that is inconsistent with uncoordinated individual migration. This industry does not draw labour at random. It draws on a specific and scarce combination of attributes, and it finds that combination in identifiable places. Three further findings follow from treating the operation as an employer. Its internal organisation is that of a workplace rather than a network, with shifts, supervision, training material and a documented division of labour between the operator who opens contact and the one who closes. Its technical dependencies outlast its staff: the same dialling software recurs across three years and four organisationally unconnected operations, while 282 arrests displaced nobody for long. And its selection of victims was an explicit management decision, articulated by those arrested as a means of ensuring that no aggrieved party could reach the premises.

detail.abstract: This essay examines the transition from physical currency to digital payments not merely as a technical upgrade but as a reconfiguration of value psychology, market power, and state visibility. Drawing on behavioral economics and payment-system analysis, it argues that frictionless transactions weaken the sensory feedback that traditionally moderated spending, producing a "consciousness gap" and facilitating recursive, unconscious consumption. It further shows how the migration to intermediated digital rails converts everyday exchange into a data-extraction and toll-collection mechanism, benefiting payment networks and platform intermediaries. In parallel, the state gains unprecedented capacity to monitor, revise, and potentially restrict transactions, as illustrated by demonetization and integrated clearing architectures. The essay contends that a resilient monetary ecosystem requires diversity: digital speed must be balanced by the analog reliability, privacy, and public-option function of cash. A cashless society need not be feared absolutely, but its implications for autonomy, inclusion, and systemic risk demand critical scrutiny.

title: Demand Forecasting and Inventory -Fulfillment Coordination for Multi -Category Cross -Border E -Commerce Export Enterprises

detail.title: Demand Forecasting and Inventory -Fulfillment Coordination for Multi -Category Cross -Border E -Commerce Export Enterprises

detail.abstract: As manufacturing export enterprises have moved from third-party platform sales to direct sales through independent websites, order fragmentation, the long-tail characteristics of multi-category products, and unstable lead times have all been exacerbated simultaneously. Traditional moving average and ARIMA-based methods are not suitable for supporting replenishment decisions, and the problem of both stockouts and excess inventory has become widespread in the industry. This paper takes operational data from January 2019 to June 2025 of the independent website channels of 23 manufacturing export enterprises in the Pearl River Delta as its sample, covering 4,376 SKUs currently for sale, 3.12 million order lines, and 11.8 million on-site behaviour logs. Build a multi-source feature set that includes inquiry volume, add-to-cart rate, page dwell time, promotional intensity, exchange rates and ocean freight rates. Using the Temporal Fusion Transformer time-series forecasting model, quantile forecasts of future demand at the SKU level for 1-12 weeks are generated, and these forecast quantiles are directly embedded into a newsboy-type replenishment model to form a rolling forecast-decision integration strategy. Empirical results show that the weighted MAPE decreased from 31.7% for ARIMA and 22.4% for LightGBM to 15.8%, with the largest improvement observed for long-tail SKUs with annual sales of less than 200 units (38.2% → 19.6%); under a 95% service level constraint, safety stock decreased by 27.3%, and the average inventory capital tied up for the sample companies fell from 18.42 million yuan to 13.39 million yuan; the proportion of dead stock (inventory held for more than 180 days) dropped from 14.6% to 8.1%; the order out-of-stock rate fell from 6.8% to 3.2%; and the median fulfillment cycle shortened by 4.7 days. Based on the sample structure, every 100 million yuan of export revenue can free up about 6.3 million yuan in working capital. Further analysis shows that there is a clear inflection point in the marginal benefit of forecasting accuracy: after MAPE was reduced to about 16%, further improvements in point forecast accuracy resulted in less than a 0.5 per cent increase in total cost. The actual benefit is to fully incorporate demand uncertainty into the decision-making process through quantiles. This result indicates that the focus of digital investment in the export manufacturing sector should shift from "more accurate forecasting" to "more stable decision-making", and a replicable technical path has been provided for small and medium-sized export enterprises to enhance supply chain resilience with limited IT investment.

title: Stock-Bond Correlation: A Case Against De-Risking *
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.abstract: When stocks and bonds fall together, allocators instinctively reduce risk. This paper asks whether that instinct has historically been correct. Using daily returns of the MSCI USA Index and Bloomberg US Treasury Total Return Index from January 1995 through June 2026-with forward outcome windows computed through June 2025-we find that positive stock-bond correlation has not been a reliable signal to de-risk a balanced portfolio. In every pre-2009 positive correlation episode, forward 60/40 returns were above their historical average-regardless of what drove the correlation positive. A simple backtest confirms this: the signal portfolio did not improve risk-adjusted performance in any period or episode composition-the Sharpe ratio of the signal portfolio is below the static 60/40 benchmark across the full sample, pre-2009, and post-2009. The return difference-approximately 42 basis points full sample-is partly mechanical and driven primarily by the pre-2000 episode; excluding that period, the full-sample cost falls to 18 basis points. The more actionable signal is about forward bond volatility, not returns. Positive correlation predicted lower bond volatility before 2009 and higher volatility after-a clean regime reversal that reflects the shift from conventional Fed easing cycles to zero lower bound and inflation-driven tightening. The SB correlation is best understood as a regime indicator whose implications depend critically on the monetary policy environment, not as a tactical de-risking trigger. * I am deeply grateful to Kuntara Pukthuanthong for her extraordinarily detailed and incisive review of this paper. Her comments were instrumental in sharpening the paper's central claims, improving the rigor of the inference methodology, and ensuring that the empirical evidence is presented with the honesty and precision it deserves. This paper is substantially better because of her engagement, and I owe her my sincerest gratitude.

detail.title: Cannabis in India: Combining Technology and Tradition for Medicinal Use

detail.abstract: Cannabis, a subject typically surrounded by controversy and social stigma, possesses a significant and longstanding historical background that is firmly embedded into the traditions of medicine. The primary objective of this paper is to elucidate the intricate narrative encompassing the use of cannabis in India, hence providing insights into its historical import, cultural milieu, and its sometimes-misconstrued function as a therapeutic agent. The utilization of cannabis may be traced back several millennia via the examination of ancient Indian scriptures, such as the Vedas and Atharvaveda. Cannabis, referred to as "ganja" or "bhang" in several regional languages, has historically had significant importance in religious ceremonies, Ayurvedic medicinal practices, and cultural traditions. The paper aims to examine the historical sources to track the progression of cannabis from being a well-regarded herbal treatment to its present-day repute. An essential focus of the paper will be an examination of the therapeutic attributes ascribed to cannabis within the framework of Ayurveda. Traditional healers have historically employed cannabis in India to address many health conditions, encompassing pain management, sleep disturbances, and gastrointestinal disorders. The paper aims to provide a comprehensive analysis of the pharmacological properties of cannabis, focusing on the bioactive constituents that contribute to its medicinal efficacy and exploring their possible application in contemporary medical procedures. The cultural and religious importance of cannabis is sometimes subject to misinterpretation. The paper aims to investigate the historical and cultural connections between cannabis and spiritual rituals, with a particular focus on its role in the worship of Lord Shiva. This study aims to examine the practices linked to the usage of cannabis, with a specific focus on the symbolic and metaphysical aspects rather than only defining it as a kind of intoxication. The paper will explore the current socio-political dimensions of cannabis consumption in India. The paper aims to cultivate a comprehensive comprehension of cannabis and its societal significance in India by evaluating the historical backdrop and socioeconomic elements that have led to the prejudice surrounding it. In addition, the paper will go into contemporary scientific investigations on cannabis, encompassing both international and Indian perspectives. This contains research on the possible medicinal advantages and the difficulties linked to the regulation of goods produced from cannabis. The paper questions existing assumptions and promotes a more knowledgeable dialogue surrounding cannabis. Through an examination of its historical origins, therapeutic uses, and cultural importance, individuals will get a complete comprehension of cannabis within the framework of traditional Indian medicinal procedures, therefore facilitating the development of a more enlightened viewpoint on this mysterious botanical specimen.
