detail.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being employed as variation operators in metaheuristics, generating or modifying candidate solutions, heuristics, or programs inside iterative search loops. This shift reframes variation as a model call conditioned on different types of information. We introduce an operator-level framework with two descriptors: (1) the type of prompt-conditioning information at variation time (Numeric, Symbolic, Linguistic), and (2) artifact persistence, identifying what survives the model call (Transient, Amortized, Transfer). The tutorial shows how to classify, build, and select these operators through a worked build template, a method survey, an evidence table, and a cost-aware decision guide.

detail.abstract:
This article examines Mr. Robot as a cultural legal text through which a central problem of contemporary financial regulation becomes visible: the systemic significance of financial data. It asks how financial law should conceptualise and govern the loss, corruption or destruction of records that constitute, evidence and administer financial obligations. The article argues that existing recovery, resolution, operational resilience and data governance frameworks remain principally institution centred. Even where they address cloud concentration, outsourcing and critical third-party risk, they generally assume that the financial institution, its records and the evidentiary basis of its obligations remain sufficiently available during a crisis to permit orderly intervention.

Using cultural legal studies and formal adaptation analysis, the article reads E Corp and the 5/9 hack as a regulatory thought experiment. The series condenses within a single fictional institution the concentration of consumer credit, data extraction, technological infrastructure, private currency and political authority. Its central event demonstrates that the destruction of financial records is not simply an operational disruption. It compromises the capacity to identify claims, establish liabilities, protect consumers, supervise markets and resolve failing institutions. The article consequently develops the concept of financial data as critical infrastructure, understood functionally as data whose loss, corruption or unavailability would impair the continued administration of financial obligations or the stability of the financial system.

The article concludes that financial regulation should identify and govern critical financial records according to their systemic function. This requires more than conventional cybersecurity or data protection obligations. It requires independently verifiable replication, tested recoverability across jurisdictions, effective supervisory access, clear responsibility among financial firms and technology providers, and governance arrangements capable of preventing private actors from becoming exclusive evidentiary points of failure in financial markets.

detail.abstract: We develop a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework for analyzing Maximal Extractable Value (MEV) allocation in decentralized exchange (DEX) markets under Proposer-Builder Separation (PBS). The model follows the PBS block-production pipeline from uninformed DEX-user transactions to searcher bundle construction, builder block assembly, proposer block selection, and on-chain execution. Multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MARL) optimizes participant policies in this shared execution environment, and average approximate best-response (ABR) regret quantifies the residual unilateral gains found by a finite evaluation procedure that holds all other agents' policies fixed and retrains one agent at a time. In a two-pool, single-token-pair experimental instantiation, we compare a configuration with two back-running searchers against a mixed configuration with one sandwich searcher and one back-running searcher. This distinction matters because a back-running transaction is appended after observed order flow and does not change the amount of output tokens received by the original uninformed trader, whereas a sandwich attack places searcher transactions around a targeted victim swap and can reduce the amount of output tokens received by that trader. The results show that MEV-related cumulative rewards are allocated differently across these configurations. Searchers convert visible order flow into bundle profits, builders aggregate these bundles through block construction, and builder competition transfers part of the resulting value to the proposer through block bids. Permitting sandwich attacks lowers uninformed traders' cumulative rewards and increases reward asymmetry among searchers.

detail.abstract: These lecture notes explore the evolution of the digital economy toward an integrated economy of architectures. The author reformulates the traditional circular flow model by distinguishing real, monetary, informational, and algorithmic flows. By analyzing multi-sided platforms, the text examines how private actors design market rules, matching mechanisms, and data access. It revisits the Coasian theory of the firm under the influence of generative artificial intelligence and autonomous agentic systems. Organizational design is analyzed through the jagged technological frontier, highlighting the need for strategic human-AI complementarities. The manuscript details infrastructural concentration across consecutive layers of hardware, hyperscale cloud computing, and foundation models. It addresses the economic implications of data governance, privacy rights, and functional portability under Chile's new regulatory frameworks. The text demystifies the immateriality of digital abundance by incorporating the material, energy, and water footprint of AI. Special focus is given to Latin America, illustrating productive AIoT applications in commodities like mining and precision agriculture. Ultimately, the role of engineers is redefined from technical coders to mechanism architects capable of designing sustainable ecosystems.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the relative movement of public and private institutional gross fixed capital formation (GFCF) in India during FY2011-12 to FY2023-24. Using audited annual data at constant 2011-12 prices from MoSPI, it reports levels, annual changes, growth, investment shares, the private-to-public ratio and Pearson correlations. Public GFCF increased by 131.5 per cent and private corporate GFCF by 107.7 per cent. Their level correlation was 0.937, while the correlation of annual growth rates was 0.156. The results indicate common period trend movement but limited year-to-year synchronisation. They do not establish causality, crowding-in or crowding-out.

title: Macro Shocks and Firm-Level Response Heterogeneity
affiliations: Stanford University, University College London - Department of Economics and Instituto Tecnológico Autónomo de México (ITAM)

detail.title: Macro Shocks and Firm-Level Response Heterogeneity
detail.abstract:
Macro shocks produce high dispersion in firm-level equity returns, sales growth, and other outcomes. We show that this dispersion reflects observable differences in business characteristics. To do so, we combine firm-level returns on stock market ``jump" days with text about business risks in prior 10-K filings to construct firm-specific shock exposures. Our exposure measures explain firm-level abnormal returns through interpretable variation in language. They also explain most of the increased dispersion in firm-level revenue growth after major shocks and much of the dispersion in employment growth, investment rates, and earnings surprises. Our evidence yields a novel interpretation for countercyclical dispersion, highlighting the key role of heterogeneous business characteristics in macro shock transmission.

detail.abstract: Technological intangibles are increasingly important in IPO valuation, yet reliable measures of pre-IPO technological footprints remain scarce. Using pre-IPO AI-skilled employees, AI patents, and S-1 disclosures for 1,671 U.S. IPOs from 2010 to 2024, we distinguish AI-washing from substantive AI investment. AI-washing firms exhibit higher first-day returns but significantly underperform over two- and three-year horizons, whereas AI-investment firms outperform in the long run. Cross-sectional evidence supports three channels: the value premium, verification, and litigation risk channels. Our findings shed light on the credibility of technological statements at the IPO stage.

detail.abstract: This article evaluates the global evolution of sustainability due diligence requirements using a systematic comparative approach. By evaluating the regulatory developments from 2010 to 2024, a pattern of ‘structured divergence’ was identified in which core substantive elements of due diligence regulations show synergies while procedural requirements remain jurisdictionally different. Regulatory Convergence Theory is used as the primary theoretical lens to analyze how different jurisdictions adopt increasingly similar regulatory approaches over time while distinct implementation characteristics are maintained. The analysis shows that European approaches demonstrate higher strictness, reach, and Triple Bottom Line balance compared to North American frameworks, which reflects deeper differences in regulatory philosophy. This research offers theoretical insights into how global regulatory convergence shapes sustainability governance.

title: Bond Convenience Yields in the Eurozone Currency Union
affiliations: , Stanford Graduate School of Business, Columbia University Graduate School of Business and

detail.title: Bond Convenience Yields in the Eurozone Currency Union
detail.abstract:
In a monetary union, the risk-free rate cannot adjust to country-level fiscal positions, leaving only default spreads and convenience yields to respond. Empirically, we find that convenience yields explain a large share of the variation in Eurozone sovereign bond yields. Eurozone sovereign bonds earn larger convenience yields when their governments run larger surpluses. Since convenience yields generate substantial seigniorage revenue from debt issuance, our estimates imply economically large fiscal costs from low convenience yields for peripheral countries in the Eurozone.

title: The Theory of Financial Stability Meets Reality: A Unifying Framework for Bank Regulation and Accounting Discretion
affiliations: Federal Reserve Banks - Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Federal Reserve Banks - Federal Reserve Bank of New York and Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

detail.title: The Theory of Financial Stability Meets Reality: A Unifying Framework for Bank Regulation and Accounting Discretion
detail.abstract:
A large literature at the intersection of economics and finance offers prescriptions for regulating banks to increase financial stability. This literature abstracts from the discretion that accounting standards give banks over financial reporting, creating a gap between the information assumed to be available to regulators in models of optimal regulation and the information available to regulators in reality. We bridge insights from the economics, finance, and accounting literatures to synthesize knowledge about the design and implementation of bank regulation and identify areas where more work is needed. We present a simple framework for organizing the relevant ideas, namely the externalities that motivate bank regulation, the rationales for allowing accounting discretion, and the use of discretion to circumvent regulation. Our takeaway from reviewing work in these areas is that academic studies of bank regulation and accounting discretion require a more unified approach to design optimal policy for the real world.

title: A Note on Bias Correction and False-positive Adjustment in Antitrust Classwide Impact Analysis
affiliations: , Bates White Economic Consulting,  and Bates White Economic Consulting

detail.title: A Note on Bias Correction and False-positive Adjustment in Antitrust Classwide Impact Analysis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: n/a
declarations.funderStatement: n/a

detail.abstract: In antitrust class actions, practitioners have used a two-step, or “in-sample prediction,” approach to estimate purchaser-level overcharges and the share of purchasers with positive estimated overcharges. Recent literature, however, has raised concerns that the positive-share statistic, which has been used to assess whether impact was widespread across a proposed class, may be biased upward because (i) the underlying purchaser-level overcharge estimates may themselves be biased, and (ii) even unbiased but noisy estimates may incorrectly classify some uninjured purchasers as injured. We address these concerns by combining two modifications to the in-sample prediction-based overcharge and share estimators. First, we incorporate the baseline adjustment proposed by Becker et al. (2025), which subtracts a purchaser-specific pre-conduct deviation between actual and predicted prices from the purchaser-level overcharge estimate. Second, we replace the raw positive-share statistic with a net injured-share statistic that accounts for potential false positives by subtracting the share of purchasers with negative adjusted estimates from the share with positive adjusted estimates. Under standard regularity conditions, the resulting statistic is asymptotically unbiased for the true injured share, has a tractable limiting distribution, and supports confidence intervals, including bootstrap implementations that allow for cross-purchaser dependence.

title: Automation-Induced Innovation Shift
affiliations: , Tsinghua University - School of Economics & Management,  and Tsinghua University - School of Economics & Management

detail.title: Automation-Induced Innovation Shift
detail.abstract: We study how exposure to automation reshapes the nature and level of corporate innovation, which informs how innovation begets innovation. We document that firms with greater robot exposure redirect inventive activities away from incumbent technological domains and toward AI-related fields, while generating more data that can serve as an input into subsequent AI-related development. This reorientation is accompanied by higher R&D expenditure, greater patent originality and generality, and a temporary decline in aggregate patent output. Our findings show how an existing technology can redirect inventive activity toward a subsequent technological domain, all of which we rationalize in an equilibrium model.

detail.title: Industrial Policy and Capital Misallocation in Exporting

detail.abstract: Trade financing through export credit agencies is a key tool of modern industrial policy. We provide a theory to evaluate its welfare effects, and we study its causal impact on trade, firm investment, and capital misallocation by using the effective shutdown of the US export credit agency from 2015 to 2019 as a natural experiment. First, we show that the US Export-Import Bank (EXIM) has large causal effects: comparing industries exposed and unexposed to the shutdown, we find that exposed industries experience a product-level export reduction of approximately $4.49 for each $1 lost in EXIM financing. EXIM-dependent firms also experience substantial contractions in revenues, investment, and employment. Second, shutting down EXIM increases capital misallocation because firms with high marginal revenue product of capital (MRPK) disproportionately contract while low-MRPK firms are largely unaffected. Terms-of-trade adjustments and freeing capital for domestic producers do not appear to offset these losses empirically. Our results indicate that even in advanced economies with developed financial markets, industrial policy that lowers financing constraints for exporters can raise output, improve capital allocation, and generate welfare gains.

title: A Comparative Study of Cosmic Consciousness, Consciousness Islands, and the Layered Consciousness-Apparatus Hypothesis Functional, Quantum, and Indian Models of Consciousness Islands, Cosmic Integration, and Cosmic Consciousness

detail.title: A Comparative Study of Cosmic Consciousness, Consciousness Islands, and the Layered Consciousness-Apparatus Hypothesis Functional, Quantum, and Indian Models of Consciousness Islands, Cosmic Integration, and Cosmic Consciousness

declarations.funderStatement: No external funding received; self funded.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the extent to which functional criteria derived from biological evidence and major theories of consciousness can be applied to non-human animals, plants, artificial systems, collective organizations, and ultimately the universe. Through conceptual-comparative analysis, it organizes system-wide availability, selfmodeling, sensorimotor grounding, affective valuation, memory, temporal continuity, and information integration as analytical criteria. The paper's original contribution is the layered consciousness-apparatus hypothesis, according to which not every part of a larger conscious whole need be an equally direct producer of consciousness; interconnected consciousness islands may instead constitute components of a higher-order processing subsystem. The hypothesis is evaluated in light of collective intelligence, causal integration, and cosmological communication limits. Emergentism, functionalism, panpsychism, cosmopsychism, quantum-consciousness models, and consciousness-first Indian frameworks are compared while maintaining distinct evidential levels. The paper concludes that cosmic consciousness is a conceptually coherent possibility; however, sufficient evidence is not yet available for a subject boundary, working memory, valuation, self-model, phenomenal unity, or independently testable consequences at the cosmic level. It should therefore be treated not as an established scientific fact, but as an open research question.

detail.title: Consignment Auctions and Second-Best Endowments

detail.abstract: Consignment auctions combine free allocation of emission permits with centralized uniformprice reallocation. Because firms receive the clearing price for permits they consign and pay the same price for permits they acquire, initial endowments affect strategic bidding as well as distribution. We study optimal endowment design when the regulator is constrained to the uniform-price auction format. With heterogeneous downward-sloping marginal values, we characterize a unique ex post equilibrium within the positive affine strategy class and show that no fixed ex ante endowment vector can implement the ex post efficient allocation. We then derive the second-best endowment rule. Strategic misallocation has a one-dimensional allocation-neutral direction, allowing coordinated changes in endowments to alter prices and transfers without changing permit allocations. Under full consignment, the optimal endowment equals each firm's expected efficient permit use; under partial consignment, regulator-retained permits are deducted according to firm-specific residual demand weights. Along this path, allocative welfare is invariant to the consignment share until a non-negativity constraint binds, and optimized consignment generally welfare-dominates a pure uniformprice auction under an allocative criterion. When public revenue carries an additional social premium, heterogeneous firms generate a trade-off between allocative efficiency and regulator revenue.

title: TaxAgentics: An Orchestration Framework for Tax-Optimized Investing

detail.title: TaxAgentics: An Orchestration Framework for Tax-Optimized Investing

detail.abstract:
The U.S. wealth management industry holds over $30 trillion in taxable household assets, yet tax optimization remains dominated by rule-based, single-account, calendar-driven engines that ignore the cross-account, multi-custodian, multi-year character of real tax decisions. This paper introduces TaxAgentics, a multi-agent orchestration framework in which each stage of the household tax-optimization pipeline is embodied by a specialized large language model (LLM)-powered agent. Agents communicate through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for orchestrator-to-pool control and an Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol for peer coordination. The framework targets the Registered Investment Advisor (RIA) setting, where multi-custodian households spanning Schwab, Fidelity, Pershing, Apex, and Interactive Brokers are the norm.

TaxAgentics comprises fifteen agents in five pools: planning, data, signal, portfolio, and execution. The signal pool contains six specialist agents covering tax-lot selection under HIFO/specific-identification, household-level wash-sale surveillance under IRC Section 1091, multi-account asset location, gain and loss harvesting, transition management via a 200/100 long-short overlay, and sentiment-and-bias correction. A Compliance Gate Agent enforces IRS hard rules including Sections 1091, 1092, 1259, and 1411 as binary pre-execution checks. A Memory Agent persists cost-basis histories under UUID-indexed cryptographic hashing with a Merkle-witnessed audit chain.

In a historically calibrated backtest across 2000 to 2024 on a 500-name S&P 500 universe with household-level wash-sale enforcement, TaxAgentics delivers 109 basis points per year of after-tax alpha over a passive buy-and-hold benchmark, rising to 162 bps with multi-account asset location enabled and to 169 bps with the full agent stack. The after-tax Sharpe ratio rises from 0.42 to 0.58. Household-level wash-sale surveillance, which is structurally invisible to single-custodian platforms, accounts for an isolated +15 bps. In a transition case study migrating a $5 million concentrated portfolio with a 62 percent embedded gain, TaxAgentics saves $119,000 in cumulative capital gains tax against naive liquidation. A comparative analysis of eleven incumbent platforms confirms that no existing system simultaneously provides cross-custodian wash-sale coverage, after-tax mean-variance portfolio construction, transition management via long-short overlays, and an agentic control surface.

title: The Early Impacts of AI on Employment among Recent College Graduates
affiliations: University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) and University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), Anderson School of Management, Students

detail.title: The Early Impacts of AI on Employment among Recent College Graduates

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We do not have any financial relationships that influenced work.

detail.abstract: The impact of AI on the employment prospects of recent college graduates is hotly debated with no consensus on the magnitude of impacts nor even the timing of those potential impacts. Using CPS microdata, we provide the first estimates of the effects of AI on the unemployment of recent college graduates in June, July and August 2026. We provide evidence suggesting that unemployment rates are especially high for summer months and that 2026 might be the first year of widespread enough AI use in the workplace to detect impacts of AI on recent college graduates, the group argued to be most vulnerable to AI replacement. Taking an agnostic approach to defining treatment timing, we find that unemployment rates did not spike in summer 2026 relative to summer months in previous years and did not rise in a significant way relative to older college graduates or young workers without a college degree. We also provide the first analysis of an expanded definition of unemployment that includes those who report "wanting a job" which adds nearly two percentage points to the unemployment rate of recent college graduates but we find no evidence of a statistically significant increase in summer 2026 even after adding these "sidelined unemployed." We estimate difference-indifferences and eventstudy interaction models using both older college graduates and young non-college graduates as comparison groups and do not find evidence of an increase in relative unemployment rates. Finally, we estimate models in which we interact 2026 unemployment with AI exposure and remote work availability by occupation and find some evidence of a positive relationship with remote work availability.

detail.abstract: This paper studies the implications of macroprudential and monetary policies under unconventional disturbances in a multi-sectoral dynamic stochastic general equilibrium model with heterogeneities and financial frictions. I show that unrealized expectation itself generates boom-bust cyclical fluctuations. I then find substantial asymmetries under expectationdriven cycles: in an over-optimism-driven cycle, the economy goes through a gradual build-up and substantial subsequent crash; in an over-pessimismdriven cycle, it endures much more profound contractions. The main mechanism is the occasionally binding housing collateral constraint, which exacerbates the consequences of the decline in house prices when it tights in recessions. The introduction of the macroprudential policy, including the capital buffer policy and the Loan-to-Value policy, helps mitigate boom-bust fluctuations. Macroprudential policy exerts better stabilizing performance when aided by augmented monetary policy that responds to financial factors.

detail.abstract: This paper tests whether US policy acts on critical minerals move the stocks of exposed US-listed mining companies, and whether those stocks move before the information becomes public, as the hypothesis of presidential conditioning of mineral stocks would imply. Two hand-built corpora (53 events, 2025–2026; 50 events, 2018–2020), each dated to the first public appearance of the information, are analysed with market-model event studies on rare-earth/uranium and battery-mineral/copper baskets against three benchmarks. The market reacts on the day the information becomes public (+4.4 and +1.6 per cent signed abnormal returns, with abnormal volume and no drift), administrative acts move prices more than presidential messages, and no systematic pre-announcement run-up survives clustering and sector controls. The President never tweeted about critical minerals in 2018–2020. SEC insider filings show post-announcement monetisation, not pre-announcement purchases; the President's OGE disclosures show MP Materials trades timed inconsistently with foreknowledge. Two single cases remain open.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Colibrí Institute White Paper, 2026. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22778931

detail.abstract: Institutional venture capital commitments are concentrated in a small number of large firms, and screening practices centered on fund size, track record length, and brand recognition leave emerging managers with a small share of capital. Analyzing 2,471 U.S. venture capital funds raised between 2000 and 2024, this white paper finds that emerging venture capital managers, defined by their exclusion from institutional search processes, outperform established peers by an average of 7.2 percentage points in IRR, 0.34x in total value, and 0.18x in unrealized value. The outperformance holds across definitions of emerging and across market cycles. The paper examines how emerging managers configure portfolios under constraints, shows that enterprise risk is driven by fundamentals rather than fund size, and finds that funds with women in General Partner roles perform equivalently or better despite documented fundraising barriers. It closes with a framework allocators can use to evaluate fund configuration and manager capability.

title: Admissible Portfolio Optimization: Information Constraints, Conditional Efficient Frontiers, and the Price of Causal Identification
affiliations: University of Reading

detail.title: Admissible Portfolio Optimization: Information Constraints, Conditional Efficient Frontiers, and the Price of Causal Identification

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is employed by a financial institution that trades asset classes related to the subject of this study. The views expressed are the author’s own.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received.

detail.abstract: Mean-variance portfolio choice takes the conditioning information as given and optimizes over weights, so that two errors about the information, using variables not available at the decision time and treating common variation as idiosyncratic, pass into the portfolio unseen. This paper makes the conditioning information a decision variable subject to hard admissibility constraints declared in advance: availability, a no-arbitrage-preserving enlargement of the decision filtration, statistical separation and, for interventional claims, invariance across declared regimes. A lexicographic admissibility order in which no risk-return quantity enters selects an optimal information class, and the classical portfolio problem is then solved inside it. We prove existence, invariance under recodings, a value-of-admissible-information theorem whose failure conditions show that selection by decision loss admits look-ahead information whenever present, and that the two-stage solution and the joint envelope are the minimal elements of two orders on one set. Under exact separation the diversifiable part of risk is a property of the admissible class and is interventionally stable only under interventional admissibility; requiring causal identification has an explicit oracle price traded against search complexity. The estimator is consistent with second-order regret. On market data with 127 candidate drivers the condition is attainable on individual equities, where enlarging the search reduces the defect at a measurable rate, and not on pre-diversified portfolios, where it is nearly invariant to the search because the residual dependence is the common factor itself; where it fails the resulting covariance still yields minimum-variance portfolios that match shrinkage at markedly lower turnover, while discarding a measurable part of their risk, which an exact decomposition attributes to the residual share, the breadth of the portfolio and the average residual correlation.

title: Financing tropical forest conservation: Macroeconomic and fiscal consequences for developing countries
affiliations: University of Oxford and University of Oxford

detail.title: Financing tropical forest conservation: Macroeconomic and fiscal consequences for developing countries

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no personal or financial relationships that could have influenced, or be perceived to have influenced, the work reported in this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: The authors acknowledge funding received from the Oxford Martin Programme on Systemic Resilience and the Leverhulme Centre for Nature Recovery.

detail.abstract: Tropical forests provide ecosystem services of global value, yet conserving them can impose substantial opportunity costs on the developing countries that steward them. These tradeoffs extend beyond land use because natural capital depletion affects domestic productivity, macroeconomic output, and public revenues. However, these interactions are rarely represented jointly in macroeconomic models. Here we develop a dynamic macro-fiscal model linking natural capital, land allocation, ecosystem services, nature finance and public finances, calibrated to Indonesia. We show that accounting for nature-economy feedbacks reverses the apparent macroeconomic gains from deforestation. Without these channels, reallocating forest towards agriculture and extractive activities can increase output. However, when declining ecosystem services, pollution and climate damages are incorporated, productivity losses dominate, reducing agricultural and industrial output, real GDP, consumption and investment while increasing fiscal pressure. A nature finance intervention modelled on the Tropical Forest Forever Facility (TFFF) reverses private land conversion and partially offsets these macroeconomic losses. However, payments of USD 4 ha-1 yr-1 are insufficient to offset the losses resulting from continued conversion of public forest. Our results show that nature finance can support economic resilience, but must be combined with domestic land-use policies addressing both private and public incentives for deforestation.

title: AI Signals in the DAX 40: A Public-Source Benchmark of Disclosed AI Strategy, Adoption and Governance across Germany's 40 Largest Listed Companies (2026 Edition)

detail.title: AI Signals in the DAX 40: A Public-Source Benchmark of Disclosed AI Strategy, Adoption and Governance across Germany's 40 Largest Listed Companies (2026 Edition)

The author holds no advisory or consulting relationship with any of the companies covered. The study is based exclusively on publicly available information. AI-assisted tools were used to support document search, text extraction, data processing and editing; all methodological decisions, scores, interpretations and conclusions are the author's own.

detail.abstract: This report benchmarks the 40 constituents of the DAX on the basis of publicly observable signals of organisational AI readiness. Using a transparent 15-criterion framework across five dimensions – strategy and leadership, adoption and scaling, data/technology/ecosystem, governance and responsible AI, and organisation and talent – each company was scored on a 0–3 anchored scale from official corporate sources (annual reports, investor materials, corporate websites, press releases and published AI policies) published between 1 January 2025 and the cut-off date of 15 September 2026. The benchmark rests on 600 criterion-level evidence entries drawn from 150 distinct documents, all of which are documented in the accompanying evidence log. The mean total score across the index is 1.81 on the 0–3 scale (index value 60/100) with a wide spread (standard deviation 0.69; range 0.27–2.93). Adoption signals are the most widely disclosed dimension (mean 2.30), while governance and responsible-AI signals are the least widely disclosed and most dispersed (mean 1.39, SD 0.98); in 75% of companies adoption signals exceed governance signals. Only about one in five companies publishes a quantified AI target system, and only one company reports an external AI management-system certification. Three disclosure profiles emerge from hierarchical clustering: broad and institutionalised signals (20 companies), adoption-led but governance-light signals (11 companies), and limited publicly observable evidence (9 companies). Industry differences are visible – technology/telecommunications, automotive and financial services show the highest means – but within-group variation exceeds differences between groups. Rankings are robust to alternative dimension weights (Spearman ρ ≥ 0.98). The report measures disclosure, not capability: a low score indicates limited publicly observable evidence in the sources reviewed, not the absence of AI activity. Methodology, scoring anchors, adjudication rules, limitations and the complete evidence base are published to allow replication and extension. The report, dataset and evidence log are also available open access on Zenodo (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22779106, CC BY 4.0).

title: Sovereign Bond Prices, Haircuts and Maturity
affiliations: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Strategy Policy and Review Department, University of Bern - Department of Economics and University of Southern California

detail.title: Sovereign Bond Prices, Haircuts and Maturity
detail.abstract: Rejecting a common assumption in the sovereign debt literature, we document that creditor losses ("haircuts") during sovereign restructuring episodes are asymmetric across debt instruments. We code a comprehensive dataset on instrument-specific haircuts for 28 debt restructurings with private creditors in 1999-2015 and find that haircuts on shorter-term debt are larger than those on debt of longer maturity. In a standard asset pricing model, we show that increasing short-run default risk in the run-up to a restructuring episode can explain the stylized fact. The data confirms the predicted relation between perceived default risk, bond prices, and haircuts by maturity.

title: GeoFederation: A Canonical Metadata-Driven Architecture for Scalable and Interoperable Vector Data Sharing in Urban Planning
affiliations: University of Yaounde I, University of Dschang - Fotso Victor University Institute of Technology and University of Yaounde I

detail.title: GeoFederation: A Canonical Metadata-Driven Architecture for Scalable and Interoperable Vector Data Sharing in Urban Planning
detail.abstract: The effective implementation of development policies and the consolidation of good governance in Africa increasingly depend on access to reliable geospatial information. However, such access remains constrained by the high financial cost of data acquisition, curation, and long-term maintenance, particularly in the context of urban planning. Emerging collaborative initiatives have sought to address these challenges, yet they often lack mechanisms for federating geospatial datasets in ways that preserve data ownership, institutional autonomy, and systematic update capacity. Existing platforms—such as GeoNode, geOrchestra, and easySDI—support the dissemination and sharing through established metadata standards thereby promoting interoperability and facilitating data accessibility. Nevertheless, their reliance on centralized ingestion and dissemination architectures frequently perpetuates data silos rather than dismantle them. In contrast, the GeoFederation architecture introduces a lightweight, readily deployable solution that enables federation without dependence on a central server or costly data replication. Its design is based on a distributed canonical directory, which facilitates efficient metadata discovery and seamless access to geographically dispersed datasets. A comparative evaluation of Geofederation against conventional platforms—focusing on connectivity performance and update capabilities—demonstrates clear advantages in scalability, resilience and governance over conventional systems. A prototype implementation in the domain of urban management validates the feasibility of the proposed approach, underscoring GeoFederation’s potential as a paradigm for distributed geospatial data management in Africa.

detail.title: Common Ownership and Collusion

declarations.funderStatement: NA

publicationDetails.detailsText: European Corporate Governance Institute – Finance Working Paper No. 1158/2026
publicationDetails.journalName: European Corporate Governance Institute (ECGI) - Finance Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: We provide the first empirical evidence that common ownership can facilitate explicit collusion. Our unique setting, the population of legal cartels in Sweden, lets us observe cartel formation, duration, and dissolution without the sample-selection bias that plagues studies of detected cartels. Combining hand-collected ownership data with the universe of registered cartels, we compute firm-pair profit weights (κ) that measure how much one firm internalizes a rival’s profits. Higher profit weights are associated with a greater likelihood of cartel participation, predict future cartel involvement, and are linked to longer cartel duration. Firms also reduce their profit weights immediately after a cartel dissolves. However, this relationship is concentrated among pairs in which the firm that internalizes the rival firm’s profits colludes while the rival does not. Common ownership therefore complements a firm’s own participation in explicit collusion but substitutes for cartel participation by the rival whose profits it internalizes.

title: Deconstructing the Environmental Kuznets Curve in South Asia: Cross-country Heterogeneity, Ecological Footprint Dynamics, and the Fragility of Regional Turning Points

detail.title: Deconstructing the Environmental Kuznets Curve in South Asia: Cross-country Heterogeneity, Ecological Footprint Dynamics, and the Fragility of Regional Turning Points

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or non-financial interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. The study uses aggregate country-level secondary data and involves no human participants or animals.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: This study reexamines the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis for South Asia using a balanced panel of five economies (Bangladesh, India, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka) over 1990-2021, with the ecological footprint of consumption as the measure of environmental degradation. Long-run parameters are estimated by Driscoll-Kraay fixed effects within a second-generation sequence of dependence, unit root and error-correction cointegration tests, and are set against mean-group estimators that allow slopes to differ by country. The pooled specification satisfies the formal EKC parameter conditions and implies an income turning point of $11,680.87 in constant 2021 PPP international dollars (95% CI: 9,150.66-14,211.08). That result is fragile. Only nine of 160 observations lie above the threshold, all of them Sri Lankan, and in no country does the ecological footprint decline as income rises anywhere within that country's observed range. Excluding either Sri Lanka or Nepal leaves the quadratic income term statistically insignificant, and across alternative measurement of renewable energy, the addition of time effects and shorter sample windows the implied turning point ranges from roughly $8,400 to $21,800; in three of those specifications it lies above the highest income the region has recorded. A slope homogeneity test rejects a common regional parameter, and country-specific estimates locate a significant inverted U in Sri Lanka alone, whose own peak lies above its current income. Dumitrescu-Hurlin tests on first differences find no evidence that any macroeconomic driver Granger-causes the footprint in the short run; the one channel that survives runs from the footprint to income. The pooled inverted U is therefore better read as an average across economies whose income-footprint relationships differ in shape than as a regional regularity. One relationship is robust throughout: renewable energy consumption is negative in every subsample, under every estimator and in every country-specific estimate. Mitigation in South Asia must accordingly be engineered through energy transition rather than awaited as a by-product of growth.

title: The Decision Relevance of Financial Statements in Equity Crowdfunding
affiliations: Washington University in Saint Louis, John M. Olin Business School

detail.title: The Decision Relevance of Financial Statements in Equity Crowdfunding

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: The SEC requires even the smallest issuers to file financial statements, yet whether retail investors use them is unknown. I exploit temporary rules that allowed Regulation Crowdfunding issuers in 2020-2021 to launch offerings without financial statements and file them by amendment mid-offering, separating the arrival of financial statements from changes in the issuer or offering terms. Investors retrieve the filing from EDGAR within a day; within two days, net-inflow days become 20% less frequent, while days with net cancellations roughly quadruple. The effect is concentrated among offerings whose initial filing reported no financial figures. Yet in cross-sectional analyses, accounting variables add little out-of-sample information about overall fundraising outcomes beyond observable offering and issuer characteristics, and only modestly improve predictions of post-offering exits. The evidence shows that financial statements can be decision relevant to retail investors without substantially improving predictions of fundraising outcomes.

title: A Stochastic Feasibility and Optimization Model for Self-Financing AI Adoption in Rural Pathology Under Medicare Reimbursement Constraints
affiliations: Ohio State University (OSU),  and Ohio State University (OSU) - Wexner Medical Center

detail.title: A Stochastic Feasibility and Optimization Model for Self-Financing AI Adoption in Rural Pathology Under Medicare Reimbursement Constraints
detail.abstract: Existing literature reports that AI-assisted pathology workflows can increase pathologist throughput by factors ranging from 1.16 to 1.84, corresponding to approximately 16% to 84% greater diagnostic capacity in the workflows studied. Despite reported efficiency gains, adoption of AI-enabled digital pathology remains limited in community and rural settings, where financial, infrastructure, and workforce constraints can impede implementation. We developed a stochastic financial feasibility model that links AI-driven productivity gains in urban pathology departments to performance-linked incremental-revenue sharing, rural pathology capacity, pathologist compensation, and Critical Access Hospital infrastructure costs. The model evaluates whether AI financing, rural compensation sufficiency, and rural infrastructure cost recovery can be achieved simultaneously under uncertainty in parameters derived from federal datasets, published literature, and explicit modeling assumptions. In 50,000 Monte Carlo simulations parameterized using federal datasets, published literature, and explicit modeling assumptions, joint feasibility was achieved in 41.4% of simulations. The model required a minimum efficiency multiplier of 1.165 and produced a five-year combined hospital-and-AI-vendor net present value of $52.45 million under base-case assumptions. Importantly, the proposed mechanism is constructed using existing re-imbursement categories and potentially available federal grant mechanisms and does not assume creation of a new AI-specific Medicare payment program.

title: Does Trade Discipline Buyer Conduct? Evidence from Uruguayan Meatpacking Firms
affiliations: University of Chile

detail.title: Does Trade Discipline Buyer Conduct? Evidence from Uruguayan Meatpacking Firms

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by the Chilean Government under the project Fondecyt de Iniciacion en Investigacion 2025 No. 11251217.

detail.abstract: Trade in an input can discipline domestic buyer power even when the foreign buyer never competes with domestic processors. I ask whether this works through costs alone or also through conduct. In Uruguay, Turkey buys feeder cattle one stage upstream of meatpackers. Its sharp cut in purchases in 2013-2015 lowered packers' costs, a shock I use to separate the cost effect from a change in conduct. Meatpackers internalized their rivals more and widened markdowns, so cattle prices fell by more than lower costs imply, mainly as a transfer from ranchers to meatpackers. Restricting raw-input exports can strengthen processors' buyer power.

title: The Global Impact of Brexit Uncertainty
affiliations: Boston University, Tilburg University - Tilburg School of Economics and Management, Frankfurt  School of Finance and Management and

detail.title: The Global Impact of Brexit Uncertainty
detail.abstract: We propose a text-based method for measuring and analyzing the international propagation of uncertainty shocks at the firm level. We apply this method to estimate the impact of Brexit-related uncertainty and find widespread reverberations on listed firms in 81 countries. International firms most exposed to Brexit uncertainty not only significantly lost market value but also reduced hiring and investments. In addition to Brexit uncertainty (the second moment), we find that international firms overwhelmingly expected negative direct effects from Brexit (the first moment). Most prominently, firms expected difficulties from regulatory divergence, reduced labor mobility, and limited trade access.

title: Did the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act Reduce Profit Shifting by US Multinational Companies?
affiliations: Utrecht University, Charles University and University of California, Berkeley - Department of Economics

detail.title: Did the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act Reduce Profit Shifting by US Multinational Companies?
detail.abstract: The 2017 Tax Cut and Jobs Act reduced the US corporate tax rate and introduced provisions to curb profit shifting. We combine survey data, tax data, and firm financial statements to study the evolution of the geographical allocation of US firms’ profits after the reform. The share of profits booked abroad by US multinationals fell 3–5 percentage points, driven by repatriations of intellectual property to the US. The share of foreign profits booked in tax havens remained stable around 50% between 2015 and 2020. Changes in the global allocation of profits are small overall, but some firms responded strongly.

title: Workforce Stability as Knowledge Continuity: Tacit knowledge transfer across age groups in manufacturing
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Workforce Stability as Knowledge Continuity: Tacit knowledge transfer across age groups in manufacturing

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This conceptual paper reports no original research involving human participants, patients or identifiable personal data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
A manufacturing firm can replace a departing employee without replacing the judgment on which production depends. Turnover and vacancy rates record employee movement but reveal little about the capability that remains. This conceptual paper defines knowledge continuity as the capacity to preserve, adapt and apply operational knowledge through employee movement and changes in production. It connects knowledge integration and transfer research with organizational support, commitment and knowledge exchange across age groups. The proposed model links five activities: identifying knowledge-critical decisions, creating reciprocal reasons to share, learning through joint work, recording selected knowledge with its sources and conditions, and validating that knowledge in use. Its central distinction is between the availability of a record and demonstrated capability to act without the original expert. Age does not determine who teaches or learns. Generative AI may assist elicitation and retrieval, but fluent records can conceal missing conditions, disagreement or unsafe practice. Seven propositions specify relationships among knowledge concentration, transfer conditions, reciprocal learning and operational continuity. A proposed multisite study combines decision mapping, independent assessments of proficiency and longitudinal operational records. The model offers a way to evaluate workforce continuity beyond headcount while making the limits of documentation explicit. No original empirical data are reported.

Declaration of AI assistance: OpenAI ChatGPT assisted with literature organization, conceptual development, drafting, figure preparation and editing. Writeless AI Humanizer was used for an intermediate language-editing pass. Its output was revised to correct changes in meaning and unsupported claims. The human author remains responsible for the argument, sources and final manuscript.

title: Measuring Customer Churn and Interconnectedness
affiliations: , Univeristy of Nebraska at Lincoln (UNL) - Department of Finance and Harvard Business School

detail.title: Measuring Customer Churn and Interconnectedness
detail.abstract: This paper demonstrates that it is possible to construct accurate pictures of firm revenue, growth, geographic dispersion, and customer base characteristics using an increasingly accessible class of consumer financial transaction data. We develop two new measures which characterize firms' customer bases: the rate of churn in a firm's customer base and a metric of the pairwise similarity between firms' customer bases. We show that these measures provide important insights into the behavior of both real firm decisions and firm asset prices. Rates of customer churn affect the level and volatility of firm-level investment, markups, and profits. Churn also affects how quickly firms respond to shocks in the value of their growth options (i.e. Tobin's~Q). Moreover, high churn firms tended to face steeper declines in consumer spending during the recent COVID-19 outbreak. Similarity between firms' customer bases highlights one under-explored type of predictability among stock returns -- we demonstrate that significant alpha can be generated using a trading strategy that exploits our index of customer base similarity across firms.

title: More Jobs or Widening Inequality? Public Data Governance and Low-Skilled Labor in the People’s Republic of China
affiliations: Sichuan University, Xi’an Jiaotong University and Asian Development Bank

detail.title: More Jobs or Widening Inequality? Public Data Governance and Low-Skilled Labor in the People’s Republic of China

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest
declarations.funderStatement: Institutional funding

detail.abstract: The employment consequences of public data governance efforts remain largely unexamined despite the rapid global expansion of open government data (OGD) initiatives. We address this gap by looking at the staggered rollout of OGD platforms across 218 cities in the People’s Republic of China, applying a difference-in-differences design to business registration records covering 70 million enterprises, listed company employment data for the period 2009–2022, and labor dispute records. Public data access raises aggregate employment through firm dynamics, with both firm entry and firm exit accelerating and net employment expanding. These gains concentrate among ordinary workers, particularly less educated employees and those in production roles, rather than among managers.

title: From Disclosure to Innovation: How Publicizing Pollution Information Shapes Firms’ Clean Technology Development
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Asian Development Bank

detail.title: From Disclosure to Innovation: How Publicizing Pollution Information Shapes Firms’ Clean Technology Development

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest
declarations.funderStatement: Funded by our institutions

detail.abstract: While publicizing regulatory information, such as that on pollution, may enhance firms’ compliance, its endogenous effect on innovation remains unclear. Leveraging quasi-random variation in manufacturing firms’responses to the People’s Republic of China’s 2014 pollution disclosure program, we show that making firms’ pollution information publicly available induces their short-run pollution-reducing innovation without crowding out other forms of innovation. The induced clean patents received more non-self citations than clean patents not driven by the disclosure program, suggesting a knowledge spillover effect. However, compared to their counterparts, publicized firms faced intensified regulatory enforcement and experienced economic losses, highlighting the burden on regulated firms. Evidence also suggests that firms’ innovative responses are stronger in cities where environmental regulations are enforced more actively, indicating that regulatory responsiveness may play a role in the effect of publicizing pollution information.

title: Meta-Books: Restructuring Organisational Knowledge for Agentic AI Reasoning
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Meta-Books: Restructuring Organisational Knowledge for Agentic AI Reasoning
detail.abstract: Organisations hold significant knowledge capital that their AI systems cannot access as knowledge. The knowledge bases most organisations maintain-manuals, onboarding documents, process documentation, and accumulated expertise-are structurally incompatible with AI reasoning: there are no dependency structures to traverse, no role classifications to honour, no relational context to surface. This paper introduces meta-books as a knowledge management design response to this structural problem. A meta-book transforms a conventional organisational document into a typed, dependency-linked knowledge graph. Source content is decomposed into typed knowledge objects-concepts, procedures, examples, controversies, and reflective insights-connected by semantically meaningful edges such as prerequisite-of, illustrates, contradicts, and applies-to. Every node carries pedagogical metadata: depth layer, role classification, engagement time, and prerequisite links. Unlike retrieval-augmented generation, meta-books restructure source content itself, making dependency, context, and role visible to AI at the point of reasoning, and support cross-source integration allowing knowledge nodes to migrate across individual, team, and organisational graphs without losing relational context. Meta-books reposition organisational knowledge as a compound, AI-traversable asset with implications across the full employee lifecycle-from recruitment and adaptive onboarding to knowledge retention beyond individual tenure. The paper positions metabooks against learning object metadata, adaptive hypermedia, semantic web standards, and enterprise knowledge graphs, demonstrating that no existing standard simultaneously occupies the intersection of typed knowledge structure, pedagogical metadata, and AI queryability. Five design principles are derived using design science research methodology and evaluated through illustrative decomposition of a representative organisational document. The paper's most distinctive argument is that meta-books are the first organisational KM framework explicitly aligned with the cognitive architecture of human learning-integrating schema theory, cognitive load theory, dual coding, retrieval practice, the spacing effect, meaningful learning, and connectionist neuroscience-with implications for universities, professional certification, and all structured knowledge delivery systems.

title: Superstars or Supervillains? Large Firms in the South Korean Growth Miracle
affiliations: Federal Reserve Board of Governors, University of Michigan - Department of Economics, INSEAD and Independent

detail.title: Superstars or Supervillains? Large Firms in the South Korean Growth Miracle
detail.abstract: We quantify the contribution of the largest firms to South Korea’s economic performance over the period 1972-2011. Using firm-level historical data, we document a novel fact: firm concentration rose substantially during the growth miracle period. To understand whether rising concentration contributed positively or negatively to South Korean real income, we build a quantitative dynamic heterogeneous firm small open economy model. Our framework accommodates a variety of potential causes and consequences of changing firm concentration: productivity, distortions, selection into exporting, scale economies, and oligopolistic and oligopsonistic market power in domestic goods and labor markets. The model is implemented directly on the firm-level data and inverted to recover the drivers of concentration. We find that most of the differential performance of the top firms is attributable to higher productivity growth rather than increasingly favorable distortions. Exceptional performance of the top 3 firms within each sector relative to the average firms contributed 20.8% to the 2011 real GDP and 6.6% to the net present value of welfare over the period 1972-2011. Thus, the largest Korean firms were superstars rather than supervillains.

title: Does Regional Cooperation and Integration Contribute to Inclusive Development? A Guide to Policymaking
affiliations: Auckland University of Technology and

detail.title: Does Regional Cooperation and Integration Contribute to Inclusive Development? A Guide to Policymaking

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest
declarations.funderStatement: Funded by our institutions

detail.abstract: Regional cooperation and integration (RCI) encompasses trade and investment, infrastructure connectivity, institutions, people on the move, regional value chains, diverse environments, and digital integration. This paper assesses the impact of RCI from 2006 to 2023 on job creation and income inequality, contributing to the empirical literature on regional cooperation in Asia and the Pacific. Using ADB’s Asia-Pacific Regional Cooperation and Integration Index, the analysis focuses on four RCI dimensions—trade, infrastructure, institutions, and people and social mobility—and examines intra- and inter-regional cooperation. It finds that RCI improves job creation across the region, with infrastructure playing a greater role in driving intra-regional gains. But it also finds more nuanced effects on inequality: while RCI does not uniformly reduce inequality, the institutional dimension is found to significantly lower inequality at the interregional level. Overall, these evidence-based insights can guide the design and prioritization of RCI agendas, particularly by strengthening infrastructure connectivity and institutional cooperation to promote inclusive development in Asia and the Pacific.

title: Does Congress Polarization Extend to Stock Tradings?
affiliations: and Concordia University Montreal

detail.title: Does Congress Polarization Extend to Stock Tradings?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Nothing to declare.
declarations.funderStatement: No organization funded the research, except that the data on politician trading was purchased with the support from the Department of Finance, University of Nebraska-Lincoln,

detail.abstract: Measuring polarization as the DW-NOMINATE's first dimension score distance between the median Democratic and Republican legislators and using a comprehensive dataset of equity trades by Senators and House Representatives in a long sample period from 2012 to 2024, we show that polarization has a positive association with cosine similarity between Democrats' and Republican's aggregate stock portfolios of S&P 500 stocks. We examine legislative gridlock (lawmaking efficiency) as a channel through which polarization concentrates policy-relevant investment signals and opportunities, thereby strengthening the portfolio similarity across parties. The subsample test on active traders, who are supposedly more adept at utilizing information, shows stronger relation between polarization and portfolio similarity, further indirectly enhancing our information channel hypothesis. Our study, taken together, suggests that the influence of increasing polarization on divergent financial decisions of corporations and individuals, according to prior studies, does not extend to congressional stock trades, however.

title: Term Structure with Investor Tax Heterogeneity: Application to the Muni Puzzle
affiliations: Princeton University - Bendheim Center for Finance

detail.title: Term Structure with Investor Tax Heterogeneity: Application to the Muni Puzzle

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest to declare
declarations.funderStatement: This paper was written when the author was a PhD candidate at the Princeton University Department of Economics.

detail.abstract: The municipal puzzle is that short tax-exempt municipal yields match a top-bracket household's after-tax taxable yield, while long yields far exceed this representative-household benchmark. I develop an equilibrium model and provide evidence that investor tax heterogeneity is a first-order force shaping the yield curve and explains this puzzle. Investors choose taxable and tax-exempt bonds jointly across maturities under no-short-sale constraints. High-tax households value exemption most and anchor short municipal yields. Lower-tax institutions participate farther out when liability-hedging benefits offset their tax disadvantage relative to households. Because institutions value exemption less, equilibrium long municipal yields exceed the household benchmark. Household portfolio substitution carries a diminishing premium to shorter maturities, while institutional reallocation affects taxable yields. The calibrated model accounts for 86% of the 110-basis-point thirty-year muni puzzle gap. Two empirical designs support the predicted maturity pattern and contradict the representative-tax benchmark: household-specific tax pass-through declines with maturity, while capitalization of an institution-specific tax benefit increases with maturity. Policy counterfactuals show that exemption repeal shifts investors across markets, raising municipal financing costs by more than the added tax receipts and increasing taxable borrowing costs.

title: Implicit Government Guarantees and Bank Loan Pricing: Evidence from Chinese SOE Bond Default
affiliations: Central University of Finance and Economics (CUFE) - School of Accountancy, Central University of Finance and Economics (CUFE) - School of Accountancy, Central University of Finance and Economics, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Capital University of Economics and Business

detail.title: Implicit Government Guarantees and Bank Loan Pricing: Evidence from Chinese SOE Bond Default

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There are no conflicts of interest to declare.
declarations.funderStatement: The National Social Science Fund of China （25BGL093）

detail.abstract: This study investigates the impact of implicit government guarantee (IGG) on bank loan spreads for state-owned enterprises (SOEs) by exploring China's first SOE bond default in April 2015 as an exogenous shock that weakened IGG. A difference-indifferences (DiD) analysis shows that reduced IGG increase loan spreads for SOEs applying for bank credit. This effect likely arises from regional variations in local governments' bailout capacities, which shape banks' expectations of IGG reliability. Cross-sectional results indicate that the increase in loan spreads is more pronounced for SOEs with weaker bank-firm relationships and higher default risk. Overall, the withdrawal of IGG undermines the "rigid payment" expectation in financial markets, directly shaping banks' risk assessments and lending decisions to SOEs.

title: When AUC Survives but Portfolios Do Not: Leakage, Accounting Errors, and Selection Instability in a Retail-Scale Machine-Learning Equity Study

detail.title: When AUC Survives but Portfolios Do Not: Leakage, Accounting Errors, and Selection Instability in a Retail-Scale Machine-Learning Equity Study

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial or personal relationships that could have influenced this research.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study uses publicly available financial market data and does not involve human participants, personal data, or animal subjects. Ethics approval was therefore not required.

detail.abstract: Machine-learning equity studies often report predictive discrimination and portfolio performance as if improvement in one supports the other. This paper audits that assumption in a reproducible U.S. equity experiment. A tree classifier ranks stocks by their probability of finishing in the top cross-sectional quintile of 20-trading-day return relative to a market benchmark. The audit found validation-label leakage, incorrect aggregation of security-level log returns, incomplete turnover measurement, and risk controls that changed concentration rather than exposure. A controlled refit changes only the purge rule while holding the price snapshot, universe, folds, labels, test observations, model code, and random seed fixed. Test AUC changes from 0.553 to 0.551, but the probability-rank correlation is 0.762 and mean Jaccard overlap of selected portfolios is only 0.389. Portfolio conclusions change despite nearly constant headline accuracy. A frozen 12-minus-1-month momentum rule is more stable and dominates the tested machine-learning portfolio and a fixed ensemble after the ledger is corrected. Its advantage over matched-window SPY is directional rather than statistically distinguishable from zero in a moving-block bootstrap. A dynamic, pointin-time cloud implementation remains positive. A fixed-universe cloud run produces a monthly return path correlated 0.933 with the local implementation across 183 complete months. The evidence supports a methodological conclusion rather than a new-alpha claim: portfolio selection near a model cutoff can be unstable even when aggregate AUC appears robust, and implementation audits can matter more than model choice in small quantitative research programs.

title: The Lending Technology of Direct Lenders in Private Credit
affiliations: Pennsylvania State University, Office of Financial Research, US Department of the Treasury and University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: The Lending Technology of Direct Lenders in Private Credit
detail.abstract:
We compare the lending technology of direct lenders, banks, and finance companies using a unique data set on secured borrowing by the universe of U.S.-based private middle market firms. The borrowers of direct lenders are distinct relative to those of traditional lenders; they are younger, more likely to be in intangible capital industries, and more likely to be located in the biggest cities in the United States. These differences reflect the focus of direct lenders on private equity-owned firms; direct lenders have negligible impact in industries and cities with low private equity presence. The lending technology of direct lenders is distinct from banks: they have almost no branch network, they are geographically distant from borrowers, they write collateral claims more focused on the continuation value of firms after a default, and they have a higher degree of specialization in certain industries. Direct lenders and private equity sponsors match on industry specialization more strongly than geographic proximity. The findings suggest that direct lenders are not a general substitute for traditional lenders in middle market business lending, but they are instead specialized lenders focused on a particular segment of the U.S. economy with a distinct lending technology.

Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.

keywords.keywords: Critical Minerals ; WTO; Plurilateral Agreement; Clean Tech; Defense; National Security

contentType.other: USTR Comments - Report on Critical Minerals

detail.abstract: This paper develops a legal and institutional framework for a future plurilateral agreement on critical minerals, arguing that the central challenge is not simply resource scarcity but concentrated control over refining, processing, conversion, qualification, and downstream manufacturing. It proposes a narrow, modular, and reviewable agreement organised around mineral-specific “control nodes", supported by tailored pricing and market-stabilisation tools, robust origin and traceability rules, anti-circumvention mechanisms, investment-integrity provisions, regulatory baselines based on functional equivalence, bounded emergency powers, and meaningful development pathways for producer countries. Rather than treating critical minerals as a single homogeneous market or relying primarily on tariffs, the paper advocates mineral-family annexes and differentiated instruments responsive to distinct market structures and vulnerabilities. It further treats WTO law—including GATT 1994, the SCM Agreement, TRIMs, the TBT Agreement, waiver practice, and plurilateral pathways—not merely as a constraint but as an institutional design vocabulary for constructing an enforceable and legally disciplined framework. The paper ultimately argues for a plurilateral architecture that is selective rather than universal, modular rather than monolithic, enforceable rather than aspirational, and calibrated to specific supply-chain chokepoints while preserving legal restraint, coalition durability, and opportunities for supply-chain diversification, including a substantive role for India.

title: MERP-DNA Transducer Machine: A Recursive Finite-State Numerical Representation for DNA Sequence and Mutation Analysis

detail.title: MERP-DNA Transducer Machine: A Recursive Finite-State Numerical Representation for DNA Sequence and Mutation Analysis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: **Declaration of Interest Statement** The author declares that there are no personal or financial relationships with other individuals or organizations that could have influenced, or could be perceived to have influenced, this study.
declarations.funderStatement: **Funder Statement** This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: MERP-DNA is a deterministic computational method for transforming DNA sequences into recursive numerical state trajectories. The method encodes A, C, G, and T as 0, 1, 2, and 3 and updates a bounded state using a position-dependent modular recurrence. A sequence of controlled experiments evaluates baseline trajectory generation, single-mutation propagation, mutation burden, mutation position, comparison with Hamming distance, background substitution noise, repeated observations, and formal finite-state-transducer equivalence. The experiments show that a local substitution can propagate through subsequent states and that earlier mutations produce greater trajectory divergence under clean conditions. The clean benchmark also shows that MERP-DNA produces a substantially larger and nonlinear response than Hamming distance, while both methods perfectly classify the simple synthetic mutation/nonmutation benchmark. Under simulated background noise, however, MERP-DNA distances become compressed and can be dominated by noise. Repeated averaging of pairwise MERP distances does not reliably recover the mutation signal under the tested conditions. The paper therefore presents MERP-DNA as a computational bioinformatics proof-of-concept rather than a clinical or diagnostic method. An explicit position-aware deterministic finite-state transducer reproduces the original implementation exactly, providing a formal computer-science interpretation of the machine. Future work should validate the representation using real biological genomic sequences and validated variants.

title: Do Apple Suppliers Rise Around Apple Media Events? An Exploratory Event Study and a Full Verification-Protocol Case Study

detail.title: Do Apple Suppliers Rise Around Apple Media Events? An Exploratory Event Study and a Full Verification-Protocol Case Study

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicts of interest exist.
declarations.funderStatement: The research was self-funded; no external funding, organizations, or grants supported it.

detail.abstract: We measure whether 31 US-listed Apple supplier names tend to rise after the 55 Apple mediaevent sessions between 2010 and 2026, buying at the event session's official open and holding 1-60 trading days, with AAPL tracked separately as a benchmark. At the event-date level (the only independent sample) the 5-8-day holds show the largest raw excess over a same-window non-event baseline (+1.02 and +1.00 percentage points; excess p = 0.069 and p = 0.17, raw p = 0.010 and p = 0.023). We then apply the full verification protocol of the modern backtesting literature: multiple-testing corrections (Bonferroni, Holm, Benjamini-Hochberg, Westfall-Young with row permutation), trials disclosure with effective trial counts, the Deflated Sharpe Ratio, Minimum Track Record Length, Sharpe-ratio standard errors, Probability of Backtest Overfitting via CSCV, a recentered White Reality Check, a Harvey-Liu-Zhu haircut, a placebo (random non-event date) Monte Carlo test, a same-date market control, and out-of-sample attenuation. Under that protocol the effect is not confirmed, but it is borderline and underpowered rather than washed out: the raw 5-day result survives FDR (q = 0.045) and-barely-Westfall-Young (0.048 at 5% FWER, ±0.002 noise), though not Holm (0.081) or Bonferroni (0.091); the single-horizon placebo test is marginally significant (p = 0.025, one-sided; 0.022 calendar-matched); and the recentered studentized Reality Check gives p = 0.12. The baseline-subtracted excess fails every search-aware test (best excess t = 1.86 vs. the 2.77 Bonferroni-equivalent haircut threshold). The same-date market control is the sharpest result: pairing each event date with QQQ cuts the 5-day point estimate from +1.02 to +0.51 pp (raw p = 0.019; +0.47 ppand p = 0.031 against the non-event paired baseline; Holm 0.28 across the family), and against the semiconductor sector (SOXX) the supplier effect is zero (-0.14 pp, t =-0.68). No individual ticker survives family correction once the shared event-day move is removed. The forward experiment originally specified for this study cannot settle the question: on the baseline-excess series at the post-attenuation +0.75 pp, 80% power needs about 178 events-roughly 54 years at the observed event frequency. The market-adjusted series is better but still slow: at the observed +0.47-0.51 pp with a paired standard deviation near 1.6 pp, 80% power needs about 57-70 events, 17-20 years.

title: Mesa 2:1 Theory of Decision-Making A Unified Regulatory Architecture for Human Decision-Making and Outcome-Consequence Modifiability

detail.title: Mesa 2:1 Theory of Decision-Making A Unified Regulatory Architecture for Human Decision-Making and Outcome-Consequence Modifiability

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study is purely theoretical/conceptual and did not involve human participants, patients, or animal subjects.
